prep: 5 min light rowing or arm bike
Push-ups x10 at an easy pace
form: Squeeze shoulder blades back and down and keep them pinned to the bench
Plant feet firmly and keep glutes on the bench throughout
Grip so forearms are vertical at the bottom; wrists stacked over elbows
Lower under control to touch mid/lower chest; no bouncing off the chest
Press up and slightly back toward the rack; rep counts at full lockout
safety: Use a spotter for the lift-off and attempts, or bench inside a rack with safety pins set just below chest height
Never use a thumbless grip; wrap thumbs around the bar
Do not use collars when benching alone without pins so you can tilt plates off if pinned
If you fail with no spotter, lower the bar to your belly and roll it down to your hips
Stop if you feel sharp shoulder or pec pain; do not test with a recent shoulder or chest injury

prep: 5 min easy rowing or arm bike
Thoracic extensions over a foam roller x10
Empty-bar bench x10 practising your arch and leg drive
form: Set a tight arch with shoulder blades retracted and depressed, glutes staying on the bench
Drive feet into the floor for leg drive without lifting your hips
Take a big breath and brace before unracking; hold it through the descent
Touch the bar to the chest with a controlled pause, then press
Rep counts at full elbow lockout with glutes, head and shoulders still on the bench
safety: Have a spotter hand off and stand by on every heavy attempt, or use safety pins set just below chest height
Wrap thumbs around the bar; thumbless grip can let the bar slip onto your chest or neck
Ease into the arch gradually if your lower back is not used to it; stop if it cramps or hurts
Without a spotter, skip collars so you can dump plates if pinned
Do not test with shoulder, pec or lower-back pain or a recent injury

prep: 5 min light arm bike or rowing
form: Grip about shoulder width; going narrower stresses the wrists
Keep elbows tucked close to your sides as you lower
Touch the lower chest under control; no bounce
Keep shoulder blades pinned and feet planted
Rep counts at full lockout
safety: Use a spotter or safety pins set just below chest height
Wrap thumbs around the bar; the narrow grip makes the bar easier to roll
Stop for wrist, elbow or shoulder pain; elbows take high load here
Without a spotter, skip collars so plates can be tipped off if pinned
Do not test with elbow tendon pain or a recent shoulder injury

prep: 5 min light rowing or arm bike
Band external rotations x12 each arm
form: Set the bench to about 30-45 degrees and sit so the bar unracks over your upper chest
Retract shoulder blades and keep hips on the seat
Lower to the upper chest just below the collarbones with forearms vertical
Press straight up over the shoulders; rep counts at lockout
safety: Use a spotter for lift-off and attempts, or a rack with safety arms set just below the bottom position
Check the bench angle pin and seat are locked before loading
Wrap thumbs around the bar
Stop for sharp front-shoulder pain; do not test with a recent shoulder injury

prep: 5 min light rowing or arm bike
form: Lock your legs securely under the foot pads before unracking
Retract shoulder blades and keep them pinned
Lower under control to the lower chest; no bounce
Press straight up to full lockout
safety: Always use a spotter; getting out from under a stuck bar on a decline is very hard
Check the leg pads and bench are secure and stable before loading
Wrap thumbs around the bar; the bar can roll toward your face if you lose grip
Sit up slowly after the set to avoid dizziness
Do not test with high blood pressure, shoulder pain or a recent injury

prep: Leg swings x10 each direction per leg
Bodyweight squats x10 with a pause at the bottom
Hip airplanes or 90/90 hip switches x5 each side
form: Set the bar on your upper back, grip tight and pull elbows down to lock it in
Big breath and brace your core before each descent
Knees track over toes; keep the whole foot on the floor
Squat to at least hip crease level with the knee (parallel) with a neutral spine
Rep counts when you stand fully upright with hips and knees locked
safety: Squat inside a rack with safety pins set just below your bottom position
Use collars on both sides of the bar
If you fail, sit down to the pins or dump the bar backward while stepping forward
Set the J-hooks just below shoulder height so you do not tiptoe to rerack
Stop if your lower back rounds or you feel knee or back pain; do not test with a recent back injury

prep: Ankle dorsiflexion rocks x10 each side
Goblet squat hold at the bottom for 30 s
form: Brace hard before each rep and keep the bar over mid-foot
Descend under control to full depth while keeping a neutral lower back
Knees travel forward over toes and stay in line with the feet
Drive up without letting the hips shoot up first
Rep counts at full standing lockout
safety: Squat in a rack with safety pins set just below your deepest position
Use collars on both sides
Only go as deep as you can without your lower back rounding (butt wink)
Practice bailing onto the pins with a light weight first
Stop for knee or back pain; do not test with a recent back or knee injury

prep: Wrist and lat stretches for the front rack, 30 s each
Ankle dorsiflexion rocks x10 each side
form: Rest the bar on the front shoulders, elbows high, bar touching the throat lightly
Brace hard and keep the torso upright throughout
Knees forward and out over toes; squat to at least parallel
Keep elbows up out of the bottom so the bar does not roll forward
Rep counts at full standing lockout
safety: Squat inside a rack with safety pins just below your bottom position
Use collars on both sides
If you fail, push the bar forward off your shoulders and step back; let it fall onto the pins
Stop if your elbows drop and your upper back rounds
Do not test with wrist pain or a recent back injury

prep: Front-rack wrist and lat stretches, 30 s each
Ankle dorsiflexion rocks x10 each side
form: Clean grip just outside shoulders, fingertips under the bar, elbows high
Brace and keep the torso upright
Squat to at least parallel with knees tracking over toes
Drive elbows up as you stand; rep counts at full lockout
safety: Squat inside a rack with safety pins set just below the bottom position
Use collars on both sides
To bail, open your fingers and push the bar forward while stepping back
Stop for wrist pain or if your elbows collapse
Do not test with a recent wrist or back injury

prep: Ankle dorsiflexion rocks x10 each side
form: Hold the kettlebell by the horns tight against your chest
Keep chest up and spine neutral
Squat between your knees with knees tracking over toes
Rep counts at full depth and full standing lockout
safety: A heavy kettlebell is hard to hold; your upper body may limit the lift, so stop when you cannot keep it tight to your chest
Lift the bell from the floor with a hinge, not a rounded back
If you cannot stand, lower the bell to the floor between your feet rather than dropping it
Prefer a 3-5 rep test over a true 1RM; stop at the first form breakdown
Stop for knee or back pain

prep: Hip hinges with a dowel x10
form: Bar over mid-foot, shins near the bar, hips between knees and shoulders
Pull the slack out of the bar and brace before it leaves the floor
Keep a neutral spine and the bar close to your legs the whole way
Rep counts at lockout: hips and knees straight, shoulders upright, no hitching
safety: Use bumper plates if available and collars on both sides
Stop the attempt immediately if your lower back rounds
Failing is safe: just lower or drop the bar under control; do not twist
Use chalk or straps rather than over-gripping; check the floor is not slippery
Do not test with a recent back injury or any radiating leg pain

prep: Hamstring sweeps or leg swings x10 each leg
form: Start standing with the bar; soft knees that stay fixed
Push hips back and slide the bar down the thighs with a neutral back
Lower only as far as your hamstrings allow without the back rounding
Rep counts on return to full upright standing
safety: A true 1RM is not advisable on RDLs; prefer a 3-5 rep test and stop at the first form breakdown
Use collars, and take the bar from a rack at hip height
If your lower back rounds, end the set and set the bar down
Stop for sharp hamstring or back pain; do not test with a hamstring strain

prep: Empty-bar clean pulls and high pulls x5
form: Start like a deadlift with a neutral back and bar over mid-foot
Keep the bar close and fully extend hips before pulling under
Meet the bar with fast elbows into a front rack
Rep counts when you catch above parallel and stand up with control
safety: Use bumper plates and a clear platform; never use iron plates on a dropped bar
Miss forward by pushing the bar away and stepping back; let it drop
Do not try to save a bad catch with your wrists or back
Only test this if you can already clean with consistent technique; stop if technique breaks down
Do not test with wrist, elbow or back pain

prep: Hip flexor stretch 30 s each side
Bodyweight single-leg hip thrusts x8 each side
form: Upper back on a stable bench at the shoulder-blade line
Use a bar pad and keep the bar over your hip crease
Feet flat, shins vertical at the top
Tuck the chin and ribs down; drive through the heels
Rep counts at full hip extension without arching the lower back
safety: Brace the bench against a wall or rack so it cannot slide
Use a thick bar pad to protect your hips
Use collars so plates do not shift
If you fail, lower the hips and roll the bar off forward over your thighs
Stop if you feel lower-back strain rather than glutes; prefer a 3-5 rep test

form: Grip just outside shoulders with forearms vertical
Squeeze glutes and brace so your lower back does not arch
Move your head back and press the bar in a straight line
Rep counts when arms lock out with the bar over mid-foot and no leg drive
safety: Use a rack set at upper-chest height and collars on the bar
If you fail, lower the bar back to your shoulders or step back and let it fall forward away from your body
Stop if you lean back excessively or feel lower-back pain
Do not test with shoulder impingement pain or a recent shoulder injury

form: Hinge to about 45 degrees with a flat back and soft knees
Brace hard; your torso angle should not change during the rep
Pull the bar to the lower ribs, elbows back
Rep counts when the bar touches the torso without jerking the hips
safety: A true 1RM is not advisable; prefer a 3-5 rep test and stop at the first form breakdown
Use collars and pick up the bar with a proper deadlift
Stop the set if your lower back rounds or you start using body momentum
Do not test with a recent back injury

form: Stand tall holding the bar at arm's length, slightly wider than shoulder width
Shrug straight up toward the ears
Do not roll the shoulders
Rep counts at a full shrug with a brief hold
safety: Take the bar from a rack at mid-thigh rather than deadlifting it from the floor
Use straps if grip limits you; keep collars on
Prefer a 3-5 rep test; stop when you can no longer get a full shrug
Stop for neck pain or numbness/tingling in the arms

prep: Hip flexor stretch 30 s each side
form: Keep the torso upright and core braced
Step out far enough that the front shin stays roughly vertical
Lower until the back knee nearly touches the floor
Rep counts when you push back to a full stand with both legs
safety: Work in a rack with safety pins set at a height that catches a failed rep
Balance is the limiting factor; prefer a 3-5 rep test over a true 1RM
Use collars on the bar
Stop if you wobble or your knee caves inward
Do not test with knee or hip pain

prep: 5 min light rowing or arm bike
Band external rotations x12 each arm
form: Keep shoulder blades pinned and feet planted
Lower until dumbbells are at chest level with elbows about 45 degrees from the body
Press up over the shoulders without clashing the dumbbells
Rep counts at full lockout on both sides
safety: Kick dumbbells up off your knees as you lie back; to finish, bring them to your chest and sit up or lower them to the floor slowly.
Never drop the dumbbells out to the sides from the top; lower them to your chest first
A spotter should spot at the wrists, not the elbows
Check dumbbell heads are tight on adjustable sets
Stop for shoulder pain; do not test with a recent shoulder injury

prep: Band external rotations x12 each arm
form: Set the bench to about 30-45 degrees and lock it
Retract shoulder blades and keep hips on the seat
Lower dumbbells to upper-chest level with elbows slightly tucked
Rep counts at full lockout on both arms
safety: Kick dumbbells up off your knees as you lie back; to finish, bring them to your chest and sit up or lower them to the floor slowly.
Lower the dumbbells to your chest before getting off the bench; do not drop them beside your shoulders
Have a spotter assist at the wrists for heavy attempts
Stop for sharp front-shoulder pain

form: Keep a slight, fixed bend in the elbows
Lower in a wide arc to chest level only
Keep shoulder blades back and down
Rep counts when dumbbells return over the chest under control
safety: A true 1RM is not advisable here; prefer a heavy single with perfect form or a 3-5 rep test, and stop at the first form breakdown.
Heavy flyes put a big stretch on the pec and front shoulder; never go below chest level
Get dumbbells into place by lying back with them on your chest, and press them up first
Stop immediately for any pec or shoulder pain

form: Support with one hand and knee on the bench, back flat
Pull the dumbbell to your hip, elbow close to the body
Avoid twisting the torso to cheat the weight up
Rep counts when the dumbbell reaches the torso and lowers under control
safety: Prefer a 3-5 rep test over a true 1RM; stop at the first form breakdown
Pick the dumbbell up off the floor or rack with a neutral spine
Use straps if grip limits you
Stop if your lower back twists or rounds; do not test with a recent back injury

form: Slight bend in the elbows, lead with the elbows
Raise to about shoulder height, no higher
No swinging or leaning back
Rep counts when arms reach shoulder height under control
safety: A true 1RM is not advisable here; prefer a heavy single with perfect form or a 3-5 rep test, and stop at the first form breakdown.
Shoulders are at risk; stop at any pinching or sharp pain
Pick dumbbells up from the rack with a neutral back
Do not test with shoulder impingement or a rotator cuff injury

form: Elbows pinned at your sides
Curl through a full range from straight arms to the top
No swinging the torso or shoulders
Rep counts at full contraction with arms lowered under control
safety: A true 1RM is not advisable here; prefer a heavy single with perfect form or a 3-5 rep test, and stop at the first form breakdown.
The biceps tendon is at risk; stop immediately at any sharp pain in the elbow crease
Pick up and put down dumbbells with a neutral back
Do not test with elbow pain

prep: Light alternating curls x10 each arm
form: Elbows pinned at the sides
Supinate (turn palm up) as you curl
Complete each arm's rep fully before the other starts
No body swing; rep counts on each arm through full range
safety: A true 1RM is not advisable here; prefer a heavy single with perfect form or a 3-5 rep test, and stop at the first form breakdown.
Stop immediately at sharp pain in the elbow crease (biceps tendon)
Keep the resting dumbbell steady at your side
Do not test with elbow or wrist pain

form: Neutral grip, palms facing each other
Elbows fixed at the sides
Curl through full range without swinging
Rep counts at the top with a controlled lowering
safety: A true 1RM is not advisable here; prefer a heavy single with perfect form or a 3-5 rep test, and stop at the first form breakdown.
Stop at any sharp elbow or forearm pain
Handle dumbbells with a neutral back when picking them up
Do not test with tennis or golfer's elbow flare-ups

prep: Light alternating hammer curls x10 each arm
form: Neutral grip, palms facing in
Elbows fixed at the sides
Alternate arms with a full rep each side
No torso swing; rep counts on each arm
safety: A true 1RM is not advisable here; prefer a heavy single with perfect form or a 3-5 rep test, and stop at the first form breakdown.
Stop at any sharp elbow or forearm pain
Keep the inactive dumbbell controlled at your side
Do not test with elbow tendon pain

form: Stand tall with dumbbells at your sides
Shrug straight up toward the ears
Do not roll the shoulders
Rep counts at a full shrug with a brief hold
safety: Pick dumbbells up with a hip hinge and neutral back, not a rounded back
Prefer a 3-5 rep test; stop when you can no longer get a full shrug
Use straps if grip limits you
Stop for neck pain or arm numbness or tingling

prep: Hip flexor stretch 30 s each side
form: Torso upright, dumbbells hanging at your sides
Step long enough that the front shin is near vertical
Lower until the back knee nearly touches the floor
Rep counts when you return to a full stand
safety: Balance and grip limit this; prefer a 3-5 rep test over a true 1RM
If you lose balance, drop the dumbbells to the sides away from your feet
Use a clear area free of obstacles
Stop if your knee caves inward or you feel knee pain

prep: Bodyweight split squats x8 each leg
Hip flexor stretch 30 s each side
Ankle dorsiflexion rocks x10 each side
form: Set a stable split stance, feet hip-width apart
Torso upright, lower straight down
Back knee nearly touches the floor
Rep counts on return to the top without moving the feet
safety: Prefer a 3-5 rep test per leg over a true 1RM
If you lose balance, release the dumbbells to the sides
Pick up the dumbbells with a neutral back before setting your stance
Stop for knee pain or if the front knee caves in

form: Shoulder-width underhand grip
Elbows pinned at your sides
Curl from full extension to the top
Rep counts without swinging the hips or leaning back
safety: A true 1RM is not advisable here; prefer a heavy single with perfect form or a 3-5 rep test, and stop at the first form breakdown.
Stop at sharp elbow-crease pain; the biceps tendon is at risk
Use collars on the bar
Do not test with wrist or elbow pain

form: Armpits snug over the top of the pad, upper arms flat on it
Lower under control to near-full extension
Curl up without lifting elbows off the pad
Rep counts at the top with a controlled lowering
safety: A true 1RM is not advisable here; prefer a heavy single with perfect form or a 3-5 rep test, and stop at the first form breakdown.
The bottom stretch puts high stress on the biceps tendon; never let the bar drop into lockout
Have a partner hand you the bar or use the front rest
Use collars on the bar
Stop at any sharp elbow pain

form: Grip the angled handles
Elbows fixed at your sides
Full range from straight arms to the top
Rep counts without body swing
safety: A true 1RM is not advisable here; prefer a heavy single with perfect form or a 3-5 rep test, and stop at the first form breakdown.
Stop at sharp elbow-crease pain
Use collars on the bar
Do not test with wrist or elbow pain

form: Upper arms vertical and fixed
Elbows tucked; do not flare
Lower slowly toward the forehead
Rep counts at full elbow lockout
safety: A true 1RM is not advisable here; prefer a heavy single with perfect form or a 3-5 rep test, and stop at the first form breakdown.
Always use a spotter; failing puts the bar on your face
Use collars on the bar
Stop at any elbow pain; elbows take very high stress here
If you fail without a spotter, bend the elbows and lower the bar behind your head to the floor or to your chest

form: Upper arms angled slightly back and fixed
Elbows stay narrow
Lower under control to the forehead or just behind the head
Rep counts at full lockout
safety: A true 1RM is not advisable here; prefer a heavy single with perfect form or a 3-5 rep test, and stop at the first form breakdown.
Use a spotter; a failed rep lands on your head
Use collars on the bar
Stop at any elbow pain
Do not test with elbow tendon pain

form: Balls of feet on the block, heels free
Knees kept with a slight bend; no knee bend during the rep
Lower slowly to a full stretch
Rep counts at full ankle extension, no bouncing
safety: Set the shoulder pad so you start nearly upright with knees slightly bent
Prefer a 3-5 rep test over a true 1RM; stop at the first form breakdown
Control the stretch; bouncing at the bottom risks Achilles injury
Ensure feet are secure on the block before loading
Stop at any Achilles or calf pain

form: Feet shoulder-width, flat on the platform
Lower until knees are about 90 degrees without the hips lifting
Knees track over toes
Rep counts when knees are straight but not hard-locked
safety: Set the safety stops so the sled cannot come down lower than your safe range
Never lock the knees hard at the top
Keep the safety catches in reach and engage them before getting out
Stop if your lower back rounds off the seat
Do not test with knee or back pain

form: Align knees with the machine's pivot point
Set the shin pad just above the ankles
Full extension at the top under control
Rep counts on full lockout
safety: A true 1RM is not advisable here; prefer a heavy single with perfect form or a 3-5 rep test, and stop at the first form breakdown.
Knees are at risk; stop for any knee pain
Adjust seat back so the knee lines up with the axis
Control the lowering; do not let the stack slam
Do not test with knee injuries

form: Knees just off the pad edge and aligned with the axis
Pad just above the heels
Hips stay on the bench
Rep counts at full flexion with a controlled lowering
safety: A true 1RM is not advisable here; prefer a heavy single with perfect form or a 3-5 rep test, and stop at the first form breakdown.
Hamstrings can strain at max loads; stop at any sharp pain
Set pad and pin before loading
Do not test with a recent hamstring strain

form: Knees aligned with the machine's pivot point
Thigh pad locked snugly
Curl fully under control
Rep counts at full flexion with a controlled return
safety: A true 1RM is not advisable here; prefer a heavy single with perfect form or a 3-5 rep test, and stop at the first form breakdown.
Lock the thigh pad so you cannot slide
Stop at any sharp hamstring pain
Do not test with a recent hamstring strain

form: Wide overhand grip on the bar
Secure thighs under the pad
Pull elbows down and back to the sides
Keep a slight lean back; no swinging
Rep counts when the bar reaches the upper chest
safety: Set the thigh pad snugly so you are not pulled up off the seat
Check the cable, pin and attachment clip before loading
Prefer a 3-5 rep test over a true 1RM; stop at the first form breakdown
Return the weight slowly; never let the stack slam
Stop for shoulder or elbow pain

form: Medium overhand grip on the bar
Secure thighs under the pad
Pull elbows down toward the ribs
Keep a slight lean back; no swinging
Rep counts when the bar reaches the upper chest
safety: Set the thigh pad snugly so you are not pulled up off the seat
Check the cable, pin and attachment clip before loading
Prefer a 3-5 rep test over a true 1RM; stop at the first form breakdown
Return the weight slowly; never let the stack slam
Stop for shoulder or elbow pain

form: Close overhand grip on the bar
Secure thighs under the pad
Drive elbows down close to the body
Keep a slight lean back; no swinging
Rep counts when the bar reaches the upper chest
safety: Set the thigh pad snugly so you are not pulled up off the seat
Check the cable, pin and attachment clip before loading
Prefer a 3-5 rep test over a true 1RM; stop at the first form breakdown
Return the weight slowly; never let the stack slam
Stop for shoulder or elbow pain

form: Neutral grip with palms facing each other
Secure thighs under the pad
Pull elbows down tight to the ribs
Keep a slight lean back; no swinging
Rep counts when the bar reaches the upper chest
safety: Set the thigh pad snugly so you are not pulled up off the seat
Check the cable, pin and attachment clip before loading
Prefer a 3-5 rep test over a true 1RM; stop at the first form breakdown
Return the weight slowly; never let the stack slam
Stop for shoulder or elbow pain

form: Feet on platform, knees slightly bent
Torso upright, chest up
Pull to the lower ribs with shoulder blades squeezed
Rep counts without leaning back excessively
safety: Prefer a 3-5 rep test over a true 1RM; stop at the first form breakdown
Check cable and attachment before loading
Do not let the stack pull you forward into a rounded back
Stop at any lower-back pain

form: Elbows pinned at your sides
Push down to full lockout
Torso stays upright; do not lean on the bar
Rep counts at full lockout
safety: A true 1RM is not advisable here; prefer a heavy single with perfect form or a 3-5 rep test, and stop at the first form breakdown.
Check the cable and clip are secure
Stop at any elbow pain
Control the return; do not let the stack slam

form: Start from a full dead hang with straight arms
Overhand grip slightly wider than shoulders
Pull until your chin clears the bar
No kipping or swinging; every rep returns to full hang
safety: Stop at technical failure: the first rep that is not full range or strict
Lower under control on every rep; never drop into the bottom
Check the bar is secure and stable before starting
Step down or use a box to get off the bar; do not drop from height
Stop for elbow or shoulder pain

form: Underhand shoulder-width grip from a full dead hang
Pull until the chin clears the bar
No kipping or swinging
Every rep returns to straight arms
safety: Stop at technical failure: the first rep that is not full range or strict
Lower under control on every rep; never drop into the bottom
The biceps tendon takes high load; stop at sharp elbow pain
Step down onto a box rather than dropping
Check the bar is secure before starting

prep: 5 min easy bike or jumping jacks
form: Hands under shoulders, body in a straight line
Lower until the chest nearly touches the floor
Elbows about 45 degrees from the body
Rep counts at full lockout with hips staying in line
safety: Stop at technical failure: the first rep that is not full range or strict
Lower under control on every rep; never drop into the bottom
Stop if hips sag or pike
Stop for wrist or shoulder pain
Use a firm, non-slip surface

prep: Support holds on the bars 20 s
form: Torso upright, elbows close to your body
Lower until the elbows reach about 90 degrees
Push back up to full lockout
No kipping or swinging
safety: Stop at technical failure: the first rep that is not full range or strict
Lower under control on every rep; never drop into the bottom
Do not drop below 90 degrees; going deeper stresses the front shoulder
Check the bars are secure and stable
Stop for sharp shoulder or sternum pain

prep: Support holds on the bars 20 s
form: Start from locked arms on the bars
Lower until the arms break 90 degrees
No swinging
Rep counts at full lockout
safety: Stop at technical failure: the first rep that is not full range or strict
Lower under control on every rep; never drop into the bottom
Check the bars are secure before starting
Stop for sharp shoulder or sternum pain
Do not test with a recent shoulder injury

prep: Support holds on the bars 20 s
form: Lean the torso forward with elbows slightly flared
Lower until upper arms are about parallel to the floor
Push back to full lockout
No kipping
safety: Stop at technical failure: the first rep that is not full range or strict
Lower under control on every rep; never drop into the bottom
Do not sink deeper than your shoulders allow; the forward lean adds shoulder and pec stretch
Stop for sharp shoulder or pec pain
Check the bars are secure

prep: 5 min easy rowing or arm bike
Arm circles and wrist circles x10 each
form: Pin upper arms to your sides; only the forearms move.
Stand tall with a slight forward lean and braced core.
Lock out fully until the bar touches the thighs.
Control the bar back up to about forearms parallel or slightly above.
A valid rep has no shoulder push or body lean to finish.
safety: Prefer a heavy single only with perfect form, or a 3-5 rep test; a true 1RM on this isolation lift adds risk for little benefit.
Check the cable, clip and V-bar attachment are secure before loading heavy.
Stagger your stance so a heavy stack does not pull you forward off balance.
Stop if you feel sharp elbow pain, especially at the back of the elbow.
Stop at the first form breakdown, such as swinging, leaning or partial range.
Return the stack under control; never let the plates slam.

prep: Band chest-press or light machine sets x12
form: Set the seat so handles line up with mid to lower chest.
Squeeze shoulder blades back and down, chest up, feet flat.
Press to full lockout without letting the shoulders roll forward.
Lower under control to a comfortable full stretch, no bouncing.
Keep hips and back on the pad for a valid rep.
safety: Adjust the seat before loading; a wrong height strains the shoulders.
Insert the weight pin fully or check plates are evenly loaded and collared.
Keep the range-of-motion or safety stop set so the handles cannot travel too deep.
Stop if you feel sharp shoulder or pec pain.
Do not test with a recent shoulder or chest injury.
If you fail, lower the handles slowly to the start stop rather than letting go.

form: Set the seat so handles start at about shoulder height.
Keep your back against the pad and core braced.
Press to full lockout overhead without arching off the seat.
Lower under control to the start position.
A valid rep has no hips lifting or back arching.
safety: Set seat height before loading; handles too low stress the shoulder.
Insert the selector pin fully and check the cable for fraying.
Stop if you feel pinching or sharp pain in the shoulder.
Do not test with a recent shoulder or neck injury.
If you fail, lower slowly back to the stops; never let the handles drop.

form: Adjust the seat so handles start at about shoulder height.
Brace your core and keep your back flat on the pad.
Press to full lockout overhead.
Lower under control to the bottom stop.
Hips stay on the seat; no excessive back arch for a valid rep.
safety: Set the seat before loading plates; check plates are even and collared.
Make sure the range-of-motion stop is set so the start position is safe.
Stop if you feel pinching or sharp pain in the shoulder.
Do not test with a recent shoulder injury.
If you fail, lower slowly to the stops; never release the handles mid-rep.

prep: Calf stretch against a wall 30 s per side
form: Place the balls of the feet on the platform edge, knees under the pad.
Lower to a full stretch with heels below the platform.
Rise as high as possible onto the toes.
Pause briefly at the bottom to avoid bouncing.
A valid rep uses full range with no bouncing or hip push.
safety: Prefer a heavy single only with perfect form, or a 3-5 rep test; a true 1RM on this isolation lift adds risk for little benefit.
Set the knee pad snug on the lower thighs before loading.
Release the safety lever only once feet are secure; re-engage it before getting out.
Stop if you feel sharp Achilles or calf pain.
Do not test with a recent Achilles or calf strain.
Stop at the first form breakdown, such as swinging, leaning or partial range.

form: Stagger your stance and lean slightly forward with a braced core.
Keep a fixed slight bend in the elbows throughout.
Bring the handles together in a wide arc in front of the chest.
Return under control to a comfortable stretch only.

safety: Prefer a heavy single or a 3-5 rep test over a true 1RM; stop at the first form breakdown.
Have a spotter hand you the dumbbells in the down position and take them back at the end.
To finish, lower the dumbbells to your chest and let the spotter take them; never drop them overhead on a decline.
Sitting up from a decline with heavy dumbbells is awkward, so do not try it alone at max weight.
Stop if you feel sharp pain in the front of the shoulder or pec, or get dizzy from the head-down position.
Do not test with a recent shoulder or pec injury, or if head-down positions bother your blood pressure.

prep: Hip flexor stretch 30 s per side
form: Use a thick bar pad and set the bar in the crease of your hips.
Feet flat and about hip-width, shins near vertical at the top.
Tuck the chin and ribs down so the lift comes from the hips, not the lower back.
Drive through the heels to full hip extension and pause briefly.
A valid rep reaches a straight line from knees to shoulders without arching the lower back.
safety: Use bumper plates or plates large enough to roll the bar over your legs easily.
Collar both sides of the bar.
Stop if you feel lower-back pain or the effort shifts from glutes to spine.
To bail, lower your hips to the floor; the bar rests on your hips safely.
Do not test with a recent lower-back, hip or hernia issue.

form: Kneel far enough from the stack that the weight does not lift you off the floor.
Keep the hips still and fixed above the knees.
Curl the ribs toward the pelvis; do not just bend at the hips.
Exhale hard as you crunch and pause at the bottom.
Return slowly to full stretch on every rep.
safety: A true 1RM is not advisable here; use a heavy 3-5 rep test and stop at the first form breakdown.
Check the pin is fully inserted and the rope is clipped securely.
Stop if you feel sharp lower-back or neck pain.
Do not yank with the arms or neck; let the abs move the weight.
Do not test with a recent disc injury or hernia.

form: Hold the rope beside your head and keep your hands there throughout.
Lock the hips in place and flex through the spine.
Bring the elbows toward the thighs while rounding the back.
Exhale fully at the bottom and pause.
Control the weight back to the stretch without letting it yank you up.
safety: Avoid a true 1RM; do a heavy 3-5 rep test and stop at the first form breakdown.
Check the cable pin and rope clip before your first heavy set.
Stop if the effort moves to your lower back, neck or hip flexors.
Release the rope slowly at the end; do not let the stack slam.
Skip the test with a recent back injury or abdominal hernia.

form: Sit on the bench facing away from the high pulley with the rope held over your shoulders.
Keep the hips planted on the bench throughout.
Flex the waist so the elbows travel toward the hips.
Exhale as you crunch and pause at the bottom.
Return slowly; do not let the weight pull you into a big back arch.
safety: Avoid a true 1RM; do a heavy 3-5 rep test and stop at the first form breakdown.
Make sure the bench is stable and positioned so the cable runs clear of your head.
Check the pin and rope clip before heavy sets.
Stop if you feel lower-back pinching or neck strain.
Do not test with a recent back injury or hernia.

form: Stand with your back to the tower and hold the rope at your upper chest.
Soft knees, stable stance, hips stay mostly still.
Crunch by curling the ribs toward the pelvis, not by squatting down.
Exhale fully at the bottom and pause.
Return under control to upright.
safety: Avoid a true 1RM; do a heavy 3-5 rep test and stop at the first form breakdown.
Stop when the weight starts pulling you off balance backward.
Check the pin and rope clip before heavy sets.
Stop if you feel sharp back or neck pain.
Do not test with a recent back injury or hernia.

prep: Open-book thoracic rotations x8 per side
Light kneeling crunch with twists x6 per side
form: Kneel far enough from the stack that the weight cannot lift you.
Keep the hips still and square throughout.
Crunch down, then rotate one elbow toward the opposite knee; alternate sides.
Twist through the trunk, not by pulling with the arms.
Count a rep only when both sides are done with the same range.
safety: Not suitable for a 1RM; use a moderate-heavy 5-8 rep test and stop at the first form breakdown.
Loaded twisting stresses the spine, so keep the weight well within control.
Stop at any sharp lower-back, rib or side pain.
Check the pin and rope clip before your test set.
Do not test with a recent back, disc or rib injury.

form: Set the seat so the machine's pivot lines up with your mid-torso.
Fix feet under the pads and hold the handles without pulling hard with the arms.
Curl the ribs toward the pelvis and exhale fully.
Pause briefly at the bottom, then return slowly.
Use the same full range on every rep.
safety: Avoid a true 1RM; use a heavy 3-5 rep test and stop at the first form breakdown.
Set the seat height and pads before loading, and check the weight pin is fully in.
Stop if you feel neck strain or lower-back pain.
Do not let the stack slam down between reps.
Do not test with a recent back injury or hernia.

prep: Ring dips or false-grip hang 3 x 10 s
form: Set a false grip with the base of the palms on top of the rings.
Pull explosively with the rings close, bringing them to the armpits.
Roll the shoulders forward over the rings for the transition.
Press out to full elbow lockout at the top.
Count only strict reps with no kipping, unless kipping was agreed in advance.
safety: Stop at technical failure, when you can no longer get through the transition cleanly.
Lower under control through the dip and the pull; do not drop from the top.
Watch for elbow, wrist and front-shoulder pain, and stop if any is sharp.
Set rings at a height you can step down from safely, over a mat.
Do not test with recent elbow, shoulder or wrist pain.

prep: Sit-ups x5 at an easy pace
form: Anchor your feet with knees bent.
Hands behind head without pulling on the neck.
Rise until your torso and thighs form a V.
Lower under control all the way back to the floor.
Count only full reps, top to bottom.
safety: Stop at technical failure, when you need to jerk or pull on your neck to come up.
Keep the lowering controlled; do not drop back onto the floor.
Use a mat to protect your tailbone and spine.
Stop if you feel lower-back or neck pain.
Skip the test with a recent back injury or hernia.

prep: 3/4 sit-ups x5 at an easy pace
form: Anchor your feet with knees bent.
Hands beside the head without pulling on the neck.
Rise until your torso is vertical.
Lower only three-quarters of the way down, keeping tension in the abs.
Count only reps that hit both the top and the 3/4 position.
safety: Stop at technical failure, when range shortens or you start yanking.
Lower slowly; do not drop to the floor.
Use a mat for your tailbone.
Stop if you feel lower-back or neck pain.
Skip the test with a recent back injury or hernia.

prep: Scapular retractions hanging from the bar x10
Inverted rows x5 at an easy pace
form: Set the bar at about waist height in a rack or Smith machine, and keep that height for retests.
Body in a straight line from heels to shoulders; squeeze glutes.
Pull the chest to the bar while retracting the shoulder blades.
Lower to full arm extension each rep.
Count only reps where the chest reaches the bar without sagging hips.
safety: Stop at technical failure, when the hips sag or the chest no longer reaches the bar.
Lock in the bar securely; check the rack J-hooks or Smith hooks are fully engaged.
Lower under control rather than dropping.
Stop if you feel sharp elbow or shoulder pain.
Do not test with recent elbow or shoulder injury.

prep: Wrist circles and wrist rocks x10
form: Kick up to a wall with hands slightly wider than shoulders.
Brace the core and squeeze glutes so the body stays straight.
Lower under control until your head lightly touches the floor or pad.
Press to full elbow lockout.
Count only reps with consistent depth and full lockout.
safety: Stop at technical failure, before you might collapse onto your head or neck.
Use a folded mat or AbMat under your head.
Practice coming down from the wall safely before testing.
Stop at any neck pain, wrist pain or dizziness.
Do not test with high blood pressure, eye conditions or recent neck, wrist or shoulder injury.

form: Set a box or bench at the depth you want to test and keep it the same for retests.
Bar on upper back, hands tight, big breath and brace before unracking.
Sit the hips back to touch the bench lightly without relaxing or bouncing.
Keep knees tracking over toes and chest up.
Stand to full hip and knee extension for a valid rep.
safety: Squat inside a power rack with safety pins set just below your bottom position.
Collar both sides of the bar.
To bail, sit down and lower the bar onto the pins, or dump it backward with spotters on both ends.
Do not crash onto the bench; a hard drop compresses the spine.
Stop if you feel sharp knee, hip or lower-back pain.
Do not test with a recent back or knee injury.

prep: Ankle dorsiflexion rocks x10 per side
form: Bar high on the traps with chest up and eyes forward.
Keep the torso upright and let the knees travel forward over the toes.
Keep weight over mid-foot and front of the heel.
Descend to full depth under control.
Stand to full extension for a valid rep.
safety: Squat inside a power rack with safety pins set just below your bottom position.
Collar both sides of the bar.
To bail, sit down and lower the bar onto the pins, or dump it backward with spotters on both ends.
Stop if knees cave in or your heels lift.
Stop at sharp knee or lower-back pain.
Do not test with a recent knee or back injury.

form: Take a wide stance with toes turned out to match your knees.
Brace hard and unrack with both feet under the bar before stepping out.
Push the knees out over the toes as you descend.
Reach at least parallel without the lower back rounding.
Stand to full extension for a valid rep.
safety: Squat inside a power rack with safety pins set just below your bottom position.
Collar both sides of the bar.
To bail, sit down and lower the bar onto the pins, or dump it backward with spotters on both ends.
Watch for groin or adductor strain and stop at any sharp pain.
Do not test with a recent groin, hip or back injury.

prep: Ankle dorsiflexion rocks x10 per side
form: Feet about hip-width or narrower, toes slightly out.
Brace hard and keep the chest up.
Let the knees travel forward while heels stay down.
Reach your consistent test depth without the back rounding.
Stand to full extension for a valid rep.
safety: Squat inside a power rack with safety pins set just below your bottom position.
Collar both sides of the bar.
To bail, sit down and lower the bar onto the pins, or dump it backward with spotters on both ends.
Stop if your heels lift or knees cave in.
Stop at sharp knee or lower-back pain.
Do not test with a recent knee or back injury.

prep: Ankle dorsiflexion rocks x10 per side
form: Set the bar on low blocks or pins so you start from a safe height.
Hold the bar behind your legs with a shoulder-width grip; straps are fine.
Keep the chest up and back flat throughout.
Squat until thighs are parallel, keeping the bar close to the legs.
Stand to full extension for a valid rep.
safety: Prefer a heavy single or 3-5 rep test with perfect form; stop at the first form breakdown.
Grip often fails first; use straps rather than letting the back round.
To bail, release the bar behind you; use bumper plates and keep heels clear.
Collar both sides of the bar.
Stop if you feel lower-back strain or hamstring pain.
Do not test with a recent back injury.

prep: Wrist and lat stretch in front rack position 30 s
Empty-bar front squats to the bench x8
form: Set the bench at your test depth and keep it the same for retests.
Bar on the front of the shoulders with elbows high.
Stay upright and sit to touch the bench lightly, without relaxing.
Keep elbows up as you drive out of the bottom.
Stand to full extension for a valid rep.
safety: Squat inside a rack with safety pins set just below your bottom position.
To bail, push the bar forward off your shoulders and step back.
Collar both sides of the bar.
Do not crash onto the bench.
Stop at wrist, knee or lower-back pain.
Do not test with a recent back, knee or wrist injury.

form: Set the bench at your test depth and keep it the same for retests.
Hold dumbbells at your sides with arms straight and shoulders back.
Sit back to touch the bench lightly without sitting down.
Knees track over toes; chest stays up.
Stand to full extension for a valid rep.
safety: Grip usually limits this lift; prefer a heavy 3-5 rep test and use straps if needed.
Pick dumbbells up from a rack or bench with a flat back, never by rounding over.
If you fail, set the dumbbells down at your sides; do not drop them on your feet.
Stop at sharp knee, hip or back pain.
Do not test with a recent back or knee injury.

form: Stand wide with toes turned out and hold one dumbbell by its end with both hands.
Keep the arms still and the dumbbell hanging between your legs.
Push knees out over toes as you lower.
Reach thighs parallel with an upright chest.
Stand to full extension for a valid rep.
safety: Prefer a heavy 3-5 rep test over a true 1RM; stop at the first form breakdown.
Check the dumbbell head is tight before lifting it.
Lift the dumbbell from a bench or rack to avoid rounding over.
Keep it from hitting the floor or your feet at the bottom.
Stop at any groin, knee or back pain; skip with a recent adductor strain.

prep: Ankle dorsiflexion rocks x10 per side
form: Clean both kettlebells to a tight rack with wrists straight and elbows tucked.
Brace hard; the bells will try to pull you forward.
Squat to full depth with chest up and knees out.
Keep the bells racked throughout.
Stand to full extension for a valid rep.
safety: Prefer a heavy 3-5 rep test; stop when you can no longer hold the rack.
Clean the bells up and lower them back to the floor one controlled step at a time.
If you fail, stand up or let the bells down in front with feet clear.
Stop at wrist, knee or lower-back pain.
Do not test with a recent back or knee injury.

prep: Ankle dorsiflexion rocks x10 per side
form: Back and head flat against the pad with shoulders under the pads.
Feet close together, toes slightly out.
Lower under control to your test depth.
Keep heels down and knees tracking over toes.
Press to straight legs without slamming the knees into lockout.
safety: Know how to re-engage the safety handles before you start.
Set the safety stops just below your bottom position if the machine has them.
Re-engage the safety handles before stepping out after the set.
Stop at sharp knee pain or if your heels lift.
Do not test with recent knee injury.

prep: Ankle dorsiflexion rocks x10 per side
form: Set the back pad so your lower back stays flat on it at the bottom.
Feet close together in the middle of the platform.
Lower until knees bend about 90 degrees or just before the hips lift.
Press through the whole foot.
Do not lock knees hard at the top.
safety: Set the safety stops so the sled cannot come down on you.
Release and re-engage the safety handles before and after the set.
Stop if your lower back or hips peel off the pad.
Never hyperextend the knees under heavy load.
Do not test with a recent knee or back injury.

prep: Light single-leg extensions x10 per leg
form: Line up the machine pivot with your knee joint.
Set the shin pad just above the ankle.
Hold the handles to stay seated.
Extend fully, pause, and lower slowly.
Test each leg separately with the same setup.
safety: A true 1RM is not advisable for leg extensions; use a heavy 5-8 rep test and stop at the first form breakdown.
Set seat and pad before loading, and check the pin is fully inserted.
Stop at any pain around the kneecap.
Do not test with a recent knee injury or knee surgery.
Do not kick or swing the weight.

prep: Light standing leg curls x10 per leg
form: Adjust the lever so the pad sits a few inches below the calf.
Hold the handles and lean forward 30-45 degrees.
Curl as far as possible without lifting the thigh off the pad.
Lower slowly to full extension.
Test each leg separately with the same setup.
safety: A true 1RM is not advisable here; use a heavy 5-8 rep test and stop at the first form breakdown.
Set the pad and check the pin is fully inserted before loading.
Stop at any sudden pain or tightness in the hamstring or behind the knee.
Do not test with a recent hamstring strain.
Avoid jerking the weight up.

prep: Hip flexor stretch 30 s per side
Bodyweight walking lunges x8 per side
Empty-bar walking lunges x6 per side
form: Unrack from a squat rack with the bar on your upper back.
Take long, consistent steps with the front knee over the foot.
Lower the back knee to just above the floor.
Keep torso upright and core braced.
Count a rep for each leg completed with full depth.
safety: Prefer a heavy 3-5 rep test per leg; stop at the first form breakdown.
Clear a straight, flat walking path before you start.
Collar the bar; if you lose balance, step and dump the bar backward away from you.
Stop at any knee pain.
Do not test with a recent knee, hip or back injury.

prep: Hip flexor stretch 30 s per side
Bodyweight reverse lunges off a step x6 per side
Empty-bar elevated back lunges x5 per side
form: Use a stable, low platform that will not slide.
Unrack the bar onto your upper back and step onto the platform carefully.
Step back and lower until your back knee touches lightly.
Drive through the front foot back to the platform.
Count a rep once both feet are back on the platform.
safety: Prefer a heavy 3-5 rep test per leg; stop at the first form breakdown.
Set the platform near the rack so you do not walk far with the bar.
Collar the bar; if you lose balance, dump the bar backward away from you.
Use a pad under the knee and do not slam it onto the floor.
Do not test with a recent knee, hip or back injury.

prep: Hip flexor stretch 30 s per side
form: Use a stable box that puts your knee at about hip height or lower.
Place the whole foot on the box.
Drive through the top leg without pushing off the bottom leg.
Stand fully upright on the box.
Step down under control.
safety: Prefer a heavy 3-5 rep test per leg; stop at the first form breakdown.
Make sure the box cannot tip or slide.
Collar the bar; if you lose balance, step down and dump the bar backward.
Stop at knee pain.
Do not test with a recent knee, hip or back injury.

prep: Hip flexor stretch 30 s per side
Bodyweight reverse lunges x8 per side
Light dumbbell reverse lunges x6 per side
form: Hold dumbbells at your sides with shoulders back.
Step back far enough to keep the front shin near vertical.
Lower until the back knee nearly touches the floor.
Drive through the front foot to return.
Count a rep for each leg completed with full depth.
safety: Prefer a heavy 3-5 rep test per leg; grip and balance will limit a 1RM.
Pick up the dumbbells from a rack or bench with a flat back.
If you lose balance, drop the dumbbells to your sides and away from your feet.
Stop at any knee or hip pain.
Do not test with a recent knee, hip or back injury.

prep: Hip flexor stretch 30 s per side
Light dumbbell step-ups x5 per side
form: Use a stable box at about knee height or lower.
Place the whole foot on the box.
Drive up through the top leg without pushing off the bottom foot.
Stand tall at the top.
Step down slowly.
safety: Prefer a heavy 3-5 rep test per leg; balance limits a true 1RM.
Make sure the box cannot tip or slide.
Pick dumbbells up and set them down with a flat back.
If you lose balance, step down and release the dumbbells clear of your feet.
Do not test with a recent knee, hip or back injury.

prep: Thoracic extension over a foam roller
form: Lower the bar to just below the knees with a flat back.
Keep the bar close and extend hips, knees and ankles explosively.
Pull yourself under fast into the front rack.
Catch with high elbows and a braced core.
Stand fully with the bar under control for a valid rep.
safety: Use bumper plates and a lifting platform clear of people and equipment.
Collar both sides of the bar.
If you miss, push the bar forward and step back; do not try to hold a failed catch.
Stop at any wrist, elbow or lower-back pain.
Only test if you can already perform the clean with consistent technique.

prep: Thoracic extension over a foam roller
Empty-bar clean pulls and front squats x5
form: Start with the bar over mid-foot, back flat, shoulders over the bar.
Keep the bar close as it leaves the floor and passes the knees.
Extend explosively, then pull under into the front rack.
Catch with high elbows and stand fully.
A valid rep finishes standing with control.
safety: Use bumper plates and a lifting platform clear of people and equipment.
Collar both sides of the bar.
If you miss, push the bar away and step back; let it drop.
Stop at any wrist, elbow or back pain.
Only test if you can already perform the clean consistently.

prep: Hip flexor stretch 30 s per side
form: Start with the bar over mid-foot and flat back.
Extend explosively, keeping the bar close.
Split the feet fore and aft as you catch in the front rack.
Recover front foot back, then back foot forward.
A valid rep ends with feet together and the bar controlled.
safety: Use bumper plates and a lifting platform clear of people and equipment.
Collar both sides of the bar.
If you miss, push the bar forward and step back out of the split.
Stop at any knee, wrist or back pain.
Only test if you already split clean consistently.

form: Set blocks so the bar starts at your chosen height.
Wide grip with a flat back.
Extend explosively and pull under fast.
Catch overhead with locked elbows above parallel.
A valid rep is a controlled lockout while standing.
safety: Use bumper plates and a lifting platform clear of people and equipment.
Collar both sides of the bar.
Make sure the blocks are stable and the same height.
If you miss, push the bar away and step out of the way.
Stop at shoulder, wrist or back pain.
Only test if you can already snatch consistently.

form: Start standing with a wide grip and hinge to the hang position.
Keep the bar close and extend explosively.
Pull yourself under and lock out overhead.
Catch with active shoulders and stand fully.
A valid rep finishes standing with control.
safety: Use bumper plates and a lifting platform clear of people and equipment.
Collar both sides of the bar.
If you miss forward, push the bar away; if you miss backward, step forward and let it drop.
Stop at any shoulder, wrist or lower-back pain.
Only test if you can already snatch consistently.

form: Start at mid-thigh with a wide grip and flat back.
Extend fully, keeping the bar close.
Turn the bar over and press to lockout without rebending the knees.
Finish with locked elbows overhead.
A rep is invalid if you dip under the bar.
safety: Prefer a heavy 3-5 rep test; the muscle snatch is a technique drill and stresses the shoulders.
Use bumper plates and a lifting platform clear of people and equipment.
Collar both sides of the bar.
If you miss, push the bar away and step back.
Stop at any shoulder pain.

form: Set blocks so the bar starts at your chosen height.
Wide grip, back flat, shoulders over the bar.
Extend explosively and pull under into a full overhead squat.
Lock out overhead before standing.
A valid rep finishes standing with control.
safety: Use bumper plates and a lifting platform clear of people and equipment.
Collar both sides of the bar.
Make sure blocks are stable and the same height.
If you miss, push the bar away and step out of the way.
Stop at shoulder, wrist, knee or back pain.
Only test if you can already snatch consistently.

prep: Hip flexor stretch 30 s per side
form: Start with the bar over mid-foot and wide grip.
Extend explosively, keeping the bar close.
Split feet fore and aft as you lock out overhead.
Recover front foot back, then back foot forward.
A valid rep ends with feet together and the bar controlled.
safety: Use bumper plates and a lifting platform clear of people and equipment.
Collar both sides of the bar.
If you miss, push the bar away and step out.
Stop at shoulder, wrist or knee pain.
Only test if you can already split snatch consistently.

form: Start from a solid front rack.
Dip straight down, then drive up hard with the legs.
Push under the bar and catch with locked elbows.
Land with feet at about hip to shoulder width.
A valid rep finishes standing with the bar locked overhead.
safety: Take the bar from a rack set at shoulder height.
Use bumper plates and a lifting platform clear of people and equipment.
Collar both sides of the bar.
If you miss, push the bar forward and step back.
Stop at any shoulder, wrist or back pain.

prep: Hip flexor stretch 30 s per side
form: Start from a solid front rack.
Dip straight down and drive up hard.
Split feet fore and aft while punching the bar to lockout.
Recover front foot back, then back foot forward.
A valid rep ends with feet together and the bar controlled.
safety: Take the bar from a rack set at shoulder height.
Use bumper plates and a lifting platform clear of people and equipment.
Collar both sides of the bar.
If you miss, push the bar forward and step back.
Stop at shoulder, wrist or knee pain.

form: Only do this if you can comfortably reach the back rack position without pain.
Take the bar from a rack with a wide grip behind the neck.
Dip with the knees, then drive and press to lockout.
Finish with locked elbows overhead.
Lower the bar carefully back to your traps.
safety: Behind-the-neck pressing stresses the shoulders; prefer a heavy 3-5 rep test over a 1RM.
Use a rack set at shoulder height and bumper plates.
Collar the bar.
If you miss, push the bar forward and step back.
Stop at any shoulder or neck pain.

form: Set the bench upright and sit with your back flat.
Kick the dumbbells up one knee at a time into position.
Press with elbows slightly forward and wrists stacked over elbows.
Lock out overhead without arching the lower back.
Lower under control to about ear level for a valid rep.
safety: Prefer a heavy single or 3-5 rep test over a true 1RM.
Use a spotter to help get the dumbbells into position.
When done, lower the dumbbells to your knees; do not drop them overhead.
Stop at sharp shoulder pain.
Do not test with a recent shoulder injury.

form: Clean the dumbbells to shoulder height with a flat back.
Brace the core and squeeze glutes so you do not lean back.
Press overhead without arching the lower back.
Lock out both arms together.
Lower under control to the shoulders.
safety: Prefer a heavy single or 3-5 rep test over a true 1RM.
Pick the dumbbells up from a rack or bench with a flat back.
If you fail, lower the dumbbells to your shoulders or sides; do not drop them overhead.
Stop if you feel lower-back pain or shoulder pinching.
Do not test with a recent shoulder injury.

form: Hold dumbbells at shoulder height with palms facing each other.
Brace and squeeze glutes so the torso stays upright.
Press straight up keeping the neutral grip.
Lock out both arms together.
Lower under control to the shoulders.
safety: Prefer a heavy single or 3-5 rep test over a true 1RM.
Pick dumbbells up from a rack or bench with a flat back.
If you fail, lower the dumbbells to your shoulders or sides.
Stop if you feel shoulder pain or lower-back pain.
Do not test with a recent shoulder injury.

prep: Light alternating press x6 per arm
form: Hold both dumbbells at shoulder height.
Brace the core and do not lean to either side.
Press one arm to lockout, lower it, then press the other.
Keep the resting dumbbell stable at the shoulder.
Count a rep only when both arms are done.
safety: Prefer a heavy single or 3-5 rep test over a true 1RM.
Pick dumbbells up from a rack or bench with a flat back.
If you fail, lower the dumbbells to your shoulders or sides.
Stop at any shoulder or back pain.
Do not test with a recent shoulder injury.

prep: Light one-arm press x6 per arm
form: Hold one dumbbell at shoulder height.
Brace and keep the torso upright without leaning away.
Press to full lockout overhead.
Lower under control to the shoulder.
Test each arm separately with the same setup.
safety: Prefer a heavy single or 3-5 rep test over a true 1RM.
Pick up the dumbbell with a flat back.
If you fail, lower the dumbbell to your shoulder or side.
Stop at any shoulder pain.
Do not test with a recent shoulder injury.

prep: Light kettlebell seated press x5 per arm
form: Sit on the floor with legs spread and spine tall.
Clean the kettlebell to a tight rack.
Press up and out to full lockout.
Do not lean back to finish the press.
Lower under control to the rack.
safety: Prefer a heavy single or 3-5 rep test over a true 1RM.
Clean the kettlebell carefully; do not let it flip onto the wrist.
If you fail, lower the bell to the rack and then the floor.
Stop at any shoulder or back pain.
Do not test with a recent shoulder injury.

form: Clean both kettlebells to a tight rack.
Brace and squeeze glutes.
Press both bells overhead to lockout.
Keep wrists straight and do not lean back.
Lower under control to the rack.
safety: Prefer a heavy single or 3-5 rep test over a true 1RM.
Clean the kettlebells carefully, one at a time if needed.
If you fail, lower the bells to the rack and then the floor.
Stop at any shoulder or lower-back pain.
Do not test with a recent shoulder injury.

form: Place a bench under the bar so it lowers in front of your face.
Grip slightly wider than shoulders.
Press to full lockout overhead.
Lower under control to chin level.
Use the same bench position for retests.
safety: Set the safety stops just below your bottom position.
Know how to rotate the bar to re-rack quickly.
If you fail, rotate the bar onto the hooks or lower it onto the stops.
Stop at sharp shoulder pain.
Do not test with a recent shoulder injury.

form: Only do this if you can reach the back rack position without pain.
Take the bar from a rack with a wide grip.
Brace the core and squeeze glutes.
Press to lockout overhead.
Lower carefully back to the traps.
safety: Behind-the-neck pressing stresses the shoulders; prefer a heavy 3-5 rep test.
Use a rack at shoulder height with safety pins set below.
Collar the bar.
If you fail, lower the bar onto the rack or pins.
Stop at any shoulder or neck pain.

prep: Thoracic extension over a foam roller
form: Start with the bar over mid-foot and a flat back.
Clean the bar to the front rack with high elbows.
Stand up fully before pressing.
Press strictly without leg drive.
A valid rep is a locked-out press under control.
safety: Use bumper plates and a lifting platform clear of people and equipment.
Collar both sides of the bar.
If the clean fails, push the bar forward and step back.
If the press fails, lower the bar to the rack position and then the floor.
Stop at any back or shoulder pain.

prep: 5 min easy cardio such as rowing or bike
Arm circles forward and back x10 each
Band external rotations x12 per arm
form: Sit tall on the bench edge with feet planted and core braced so the torso stays still.
Lead with the elbows, keeping a slight fixed bend in the arms.
Raise to about shoulder height with the hands no higher than the elbows.
Valid rep: no body lean or bounce, dumbbells reach shoulder level together, then a controlled lowering.
safety: Avoid a true 1RM on this isolation lift; prefer a heavy single with perfect form or a 3-5 rep test.
Pick the dumbbells up from the floor with a neutral back before sitting, and lower them to your sides then the floor after.
Stop if you feel a pinch or sharp pain at the top of the shoulder; that is a sign of impingement.
Do not test with a recent shoulder or rotator cuff injury.
Stop at the first form breakdown, such as swinging, shrugging or bending the elbows more.

prep: 5 min easy cardio such as bike or rowing
Arm circles and cross-body arm swings x10 each
Side-lying external rotations x12 per arm, light
form: Hold a sturdy support with the free hand and keep the torso upright, not leaning away.
Raise the arm out to the side with a slight elbow bend until it is level with the shoulder.
Keep the shoulder down; do not shrug the weight up with the trap.
Valid rep: no hip kick or torso swing, arm reaches shoulder height, controlled lowering.
safety: Avoid a true 1RM on this isolation lift; prefer a heavy single with perfect form or a 3-5 rep test.
Test the weaker arm first and use the same weight and standard for both sides.
Stop at any pinch or sharp pain at the front or top of the shoulder.
Do not test with a current shoulder, elbow or neck injury.
Pick up and set down the dumbbell with a neutral spine, bending the knees.

prep: Band front raises or band pull-aparts x15
form: Set the bench to a low incline and keep your back and head against the pad throughout.
Raise the dumbbells in front with a slight elbow bend to about shoulder height.
Keep the shoulders pulled back and down; avoid shrugging.
Valid rep: back stays on the bench, no swinging, controlled descent to the start.
safety: Avoid a true 1RM on this isolation lift; prefer a heavy single with perfect form or a 3-5 rep test.
Get into position by sitting with the dumbbells on your thighs, then lie back; after the test, sit up before setting them down.
Stop at any pinch at the front of the shoulder or pain in the biceps tendon area.
Do not test with a recent shoulder injury or front shoulder pain.
Check the bench pin and seat are locked before starting.

prep: Arm circles and arm swings x10 each
Light cable front raises x12 per arm
form: Stand facing away from the low pulley with a staggered stance and braced core.
Raise the arm in front, slight elbow bend, palm down, to just above shoulder height.
Keep the torso still; no leaning back or hip drive.
Valid rep: smooth lift without jerking the stack, brief pause at top, controlled lowering.
safety: Avoid a true 1RM on this isolation lift; prefer a heavy single with perfect form or a 3-5 rep test.
Check the pin is fully inserted in the stack and the cable and clip are not frayed or loose.
Return the weight slowly; do not let the stack slam or let go of the handle under load.
Stop at any sharp or pinching shoulder pain.
Use the same arm order and weight standard for both sides.

prep: Prone Y raises with no weight x10
form: Raise the arms in the scapular plane, about 30 degrees in front of the body, thumbs up.
Stand tall with ribs down and core braced; do not arch the lower back.
Lift to about shoulder height with straight but not locked elbows.
Valid rep: no leaning back or shrugging, controlled lowering.
safety: Avoid a true 1RM on this isolation lift; prefer a heavy single with perfect form or a 3-5 rep test.
This is a shoulder-health exercise, so a 5+ rep test with light weight is usually the better choice.
Stop at any pinching or pain in the shoulder.
Do not test with a current rotator cuff or shoulder injury.
Stop at the first form breakdown, such as swinging, shrugging or bending the elbows more.

prep: Light plate halos x8 each way
form: Grip the plate firmly at 3 and 9 o'clock with a slight elbow bend.
Brace the core and keep a neutral spine; do not lean back.
Raise the plate to about eye level, then lower under control.
Valid rep: no hip swing, plate reaches the same height each attempt.
safety: Avoid a true 1RM on this isolation lift; prefer a heavy single with perfect form or a 3-5 rep test.
Use a plate with a good grip and keep your feet clear in case you drop it.
Stop if your grip starts slipping or the lower back starts arching.
Stop at any front shoulder pinch or biceps tendon pain.
Do not test with a current shoulder or lower back injury.

prep: Wall slides and thoracic extensions over a foam roller x10
Band pull-aparts and band dislocates x10
form: Stand with feet shoulder width, glutes squeezed and ribs down to protect the lower back.
Keep a slight fixed elbow bend and raise the bar in an arc to directly overhead.
Do not lean back to get the bar up; the torso stays vertical.
Valid rep: bar reaches overhead with control and is lowered slowly to the thighs.
safety: Avoid a true 1RM on this isolation lift; prefer a heavy single with perfect form or a 3-5 rep test.
Use collars and lift in a clear area; the long lever puts heavy load on the shoulders and lower back.
If you lose control overhead, step back and lower the bar in front of you, never behind.
Stop at any shoulder pinch or lower back pain.
Do not test with limited overhead mobility or a current shoulder injury.

prep: 5 min easy cardio such as rowing
Face pulls with a band x15
form: Sit on the bench end and hinge forward until the chest is close to the thighs, back flat.
Raise the dumbbells out to the sides with a slight elbow bend, leading with the elbows.
Lift until the arms are about parallel to the floor without sitting up.
Valid rep: torso angle stays the same, no jerking, controlled lowering.
safety: Avoid a true 1RM on this isolation lift; prefer a heavy single with perfect form or a 3-5 rep test.
Pick up the dumbbells from beside your feet while already seated and set them back down the same way.
Stop if you start lifting the torso or yanking the weight.
Stop at any sharp pain in the back of the shoulder or neck.
Do not test with a current shoulder or lower back injury.

prep: Hip hinge drill with a dowel x10
form: Hinge forward with a flat back and rest the forehead lightly on the bench pad for support.
Keep the knees soft and the weight on the mid-foot.
Raise the dumbbells out to the sides with slightly bent elbows to shoulder level.
Valid rep: head stays on the bench, no torso swing, controlled lowering.
safety: Avoid a true 1RM on this isolation lift; prefer a heavy single with perfect form or a 3-5 rep test.
Do not press hard into the bench with your head or neck; it is only a guide.
Pick up and set down the dumbbells with a flat back, bending at the knees.
Stop at any neck or lower back pain or shoulder pinch.
Stop at the first form breakdown, such as swinging, shrugging or bending the elbows more.

prep: Prone T raises without weight x10
Thoracic extensions over a foam roller x10
form: Lie chest down on a flat bench with the chin just past the end.
Keep a slight fixed elbow bend and arms perpendicular to the torso.
Raise until the elbows reach shoulder height and pause briefly.
Valid rep: chest stays on the bench, no kicking or jerking, slow lowering.
safety: Avoid a true 1RM on this isolation lift; prefer a heavy single with perfect form or a 3-5 rep test.
Have the dumbbells on the floor beside the bench so you can pick them up and put them down from the lying position.
Stop at any pinch or sharp pain in the back of the shoulder.
Do not test with a current shoulder injury.
Make sure the bench is stable and will not tip.

prep: Prone T raises without weight x10
form: Lie chest down on a bench set to about 15 degrees with the chest supported.
Keep the elbows slightly bent and the arms perpendicular to the torso.
Raise the arms to the side until elbows are at shoulder height and hold a second.
Valid rep: chest stays on the pad, no swinging, controlled lowering.
safety: Avoid a true 1RM on this isolation lift; prefer a heavy single with perfect form or a 3-5 rep test.
Check the bench incline pin is locked before lying down.
Pick up and set down the dumbbells from beside the bench while lying chest down.
Stop at any rear shoulder pinch or elbow pain.
Stop at the first form breakdown, such as swinging, shrugging or bending the elbows more.

prep: Band external rotations x12 per arm
Prone Y-T raises without weight x8 each
form: Lie chest down on a 30 degree incline bench with the toes pressing into the floor.
Start palms down and rotate to palms facing each other as the arms rise.
Keep a slight elbow bend and squeeze the shoulder blades together.
Valid rep: arms rise level with the head, chest stays on the pad, slow lowering.
safety: Avoid a true 1RM; the rotation stresses the rotator cuff, so use a 5+ rep test with light weight.
Pick up and set down the dumbbells from beside the bench while lying on it.
Stop at any pain, clicking or pinching in the shoulder.
Do not test with a current rotator cuff or shoulder injury.

prep: 5 min easy cardio such as rowing
Light cable rear delt flyes x12
form: Set the pulleys at shoulder height and cross the cables, holding the opposite handles.
Stand tall with a braced core and soft knees.
Pull the arms out and back with slightly bent elbows to in line with the body.
Valid rep: no leaning back or shrugging, controlled return without letting the stack slam.
safety: Avoid a true 1RM on this isolation lift; prefer a heavy single with perfect form or a 3-5 rep test.
Check both pins are fully inserted and the stacks are the same weight.
Return the handles slowly; do not let go while the cables are under load.
Stop at any rear shoulder pinch or elbow pain.
Stop at the first form breakdown, such as swinging, shrugging or bending the elbows more.

prep: Band external rotations x12 per arm
form: Grip a little wider than shoulder width so the shoulders have room.
Stand close to the bar and brace the core.
Lead with the elbows and pull to around chest height.
Valid rep: no hip drive or leaning back, controlled lowering to the thighs.
safety: Avoid a true 1RM; prefer a heavy single with perfect form or a 3-5 rep test.
Upright rows can pinch the shoulder; keep elbows no higher than the shoulders and stop at any pinching pain.
Set the Smith safety stops just below the starting position and practise rotating the hooks before loading.
Do not test with a current shoulder impingement or wrist pain.

prep: Band external rotations x12 per arm
form: Use a grip about shoulder width or a little wider on the straight bar.
Keep the bar close to the body and the torso still.
Lead with the elbows, keeping them above the forearms, to around chest height.
Valid rep: no leaning back or jerking the stack, slow lowering to the thighs.
safety: Avoid a true 1RM; prefer a heavy single with perfect form or a 3-5 rep test.
Upright rows can pinch the shoulder; keep elbows no higher than the shoulders and stop at any pinching pain.
Check the stack pin and cable clip before loading heavy.
Lower the bar fully to the thighs before releasing it; do not let the stack slam.

prep: Band external rotations x12 per arm
form: Hold the dumbbells in front of the thighs and stand tall with a braced core.
Lead with the elbows and keep the dumbbells close to the body.
Pull to around chest height, elbows no higher than the shoulders.
Valid rep: no hip drive or leaning back, controlled lowering.
safety: Avoid a true 1RM; prefer a heavy single with perfect form or a 3-5 rep test.
Upright rows can pinch the shoulder; keep elbows no higher than the shoulders and stop at any pinching pain.
Pick up and set down the dumbbells with a flat back, bending the knees.
Do not test with a current shoulder or wrist injury.

prep: 5 min easy cardio such as rowing
Band pull-aparts x15 and band dislocates x10
Empty bar presses x10 before the warm-up sets
form: Retract and depress the shoulder blades and keep them pinned to the bench.
Set feet flat and drive through them; keep glutes on the bench.
Grip wider than normal but forearms close to vertical at the bottom.
Valid rep: bar touches the chest under control, no bounce, both arms lock out.
safety: Always use a spotter or a rack with safety pins/arms set just below chest height.
Never use a thumbless grip; wrap the thumbs around the bar.
Do not use collars if benching alone without safeties, so plates can be tipped off in an emergency.
A wide grip stresses the shoulders; stop at any front shoulder or chest pain.
Do not test with a recent shoulder or pec injury.

prep: Band pull-aparts x15 and band dislocates x10
form: Lock the legs under the pads before unracking.
Retract the shoulder blades and keep a tight upper back.
Lower to the lower chest with forearms close to vertical.
Valid rep: touch the chest under control, no bounce, full lockout.
safety: A spotter is essential; decline benches rarely have safety arms and the bar path is near the neck.
Wrap the thumbs around the bar; never use a thumbless grip.
Sit up slowly after the test; the head-down position can make you dizzy.
Stop at any front shoulder or chest pain.
Do not test with high blood pressure issues, a recent shoulder injury or pec strain.

form: Lie on the floor with the bar set in a rack at safety-pin height above you.
Tuck elbows about 45 degrees and squeeze the shoulder blades together.
Lower until the upper arms touch the floor, pause, then press.
Valid rep: upper arms rest on the floor briefly with no bounce, full lockout.
safety: Set up in a power rack with safety pins/arms just below the lowest bar position, or use a spotter.
Lower the triceps to the floor gently; do not slam the elbows down.
If you fail, lower the bar to the pins or have the spotter take it.
Stop at any elbow or shoulder pain.

prep: Empty bar presses to the boards x10
form: Set the boards securely on the chest, held by a partner or bands.
Retract the shoulder blades, arch slightly and drive the feet into the floor.
Lower to touch the boards lightly, tuck elbows, then drive up.
Valid rep: bar touches the boards without bouncing and both arms lock out.
safety: Use a spotter or safety pins set just below the top of the boards.
Board presses allow more weight than a full bench, so build up in small jumps.
Make sure the boards cannot slide off during the lift.
Stop at any elbow or shoulder pain, which is common with heavy partial presses.

prep: Light pin presses with the empty bar x8
form: Set the pins at your chosen height and use that same height every test.
Lie with the bar directly over your normal touch point, shoulder blades retracted.
Press from a dead stop, elbows tucked, as hard as possible.
Valid rep: start from a full stop on the pins and reach full lockout.
safety: Check both pins are fully inserted and level before loading.
Return the bar to the pins under control; do not drop it.
Use collars so plates cannot shift on the pins.
Stop at any shoulder or elbow pain; dead-stop starts load the joints hard.

form: Set the seat so the handles line up with mid-chest.
Keep the shoulder blades back and down against the pad.
Press to full extension without locking hard, then return under control.
Valid rep: full range of motion, back stays on the pad.
safety: Adjust the seat and check the pin is fully inserted in the stack before loading.
Return the weight slowly; do not let the stack slam.
Stop at any shoulder or chest pain.
Do not test with a recent pec or shoulder injury.

form: Adjust the seat so the handles start at upper chest level.
Retract the shoulder blades and keep the head and back on the pad.
Press up and forward to full extension, then lower under control.
Valid rep: full range of motion, no arching off the seat.
safety: Load plates evenly on both sides and check the starting stop/catch is set.
Lower the handles slowly back to the start; do not let the weight crash.
Stop at any front shoulder or pec pain.
Do not test with a recent shoulder or chest injury.

form: Adjust the seat so the handles start near the bottom of the chest.
Keep chest up and shoulder blades retracted.
Press forward to full extension, brief pause, then return under control.
Valid rep: full range of motion without the back leaving the pad.
safety: Load plates evenly on both sides before sitting down.
Return the weight to the stops slowly once the attempt is done.
Stop at any chest or shoulder pain.
Do not test with a recent pec strain or shoulder injury.

prep: Empty Smith bar incline presses x10
form: Place the incline bench so the bar lowers to the upper chest.
Retract the shoulder blades and keep the feet planted.
Lower to the upper chest under control and press straight up.
Valid rep: bar touches the chest without bounce, full lockout.
safety: Set the Smith safety stops just above chest height when the bar is lowered, so it cannot reach your neck or chest.
Practise twisting the bar to hook and unhook it before loading.
Check the bench is placed correctly and locked at the right angle.
Stop at any shoulder pain; the fixed path can stress the shoulders.

prep: Empty Smith bar decline presses x10
form: Position the decline bench so the bar lowers to the lower chest.
Lock the legs in the pads and retract the shoulder blades.
