Lower to the chest under control, pause briefly, press to lockout.
Valid rep: chest touch without bounce, full lockout, re-hook safely.
safety: Set the Smith safety stops just above chest height when the bar is lowered, so it cannot reach your neck or chest.
Practise rotating the bar to hook and unhook before loading.
Sit up slowly after the test; the head-down position can cause dizziness.
Stop at any shoulder or pec pain.

prep: Empty Smith bar decline presses x10
form: Use a grip wider than shoulder width and set the bar where you can unrack with arms nearly straight.
Retract the shoulder blades and keep the legs locked under the pads.
Lower lightly to the torso, brief pause, then press.
Valid rep: light chest contact with no bounce and full lockout.
safety: Set the Smith safety stops just above chest height when the bar is lowered, so it cannot reach your neck or chest.
Check the bench is centered under the bar before loading.
Rehook the bar fully after the attempt before letting go.
Sit up slowly; stop if you feel dizzy or have shoulder pain.

form: Palms face each other and the shoulder blades stay retracted.
Keep the elbows tucked close to the body.
Lower until the dumbbells are beside the chest, then press up together.
Valid rep: full range, both arms lock out at the same time without bouncing.
safety: Get the dumbbells into place by sitting with them on your thighs and kicking them up one at a time as you lie back.
To finish, bring the dumbbells to your chest and sit up, or lower them to the sides with control; do not drop them across your body.
Have a spotter ready to help at the wrists if needed.
Stop at any shoulder or elbow pain.

prep: Light single-arm presses x10 per side
form: Brace the core hard to stop rotating off the bench.
Plant both feet wide for balance.
Lower to chest level and press up in a straight line.
Valid rep: hips and shoulders stay on the bench, full lockout.
safety: Get the dumbbells into place by sitting with them on your thighs and kicking them up one at a time as you lie back.
To finish, bring the dumbbells to your chest and sit up, or lower them to the sides with control; do not drop them across your body.
Test the weaker arm first and use a spotter if you can.
Stop if you start twisting off the bench or feel shoulder pain.

form: Lie on the floor with knees bent and feet flat.
Lower until the upper arms touch the floor, pause briefly.
Press up and keep the wrists stacked over the elbows.
Valid rep: elbows touch the floor without bouncing and both arms lock out.
safety: Get the dumbbells in place by sitting with them on your thighs and rolling back carefully.
To finish, lower the dumbbells to the floor beside you, not over your face.
Lower the elbows gently; do not slam them on the floor.
Stop at any elbow or shoulder pain.

form: Set the bench to a moderate incline and lock it in place.
Palms face each other and the elbows stay tucked.
Lower beside the upper chest, then press up and slightly together.
Valid rep: full range, no bouncing, both arms lock out together.
safety: Get the dumbbells into place by sitting with them on your thighs and kicking them up one at a time as you lie back.
To finish, bring the dumbbells to your chest and sit up, or lower them to the sides with control; do not drop them across your body.
A spotter at the wrists is recommended for heavy attempts.
Stop at any front shoulder pain.

form: Set the bench to a moderate incline and check it is secure.
Retract the shoulder blades and keep the palms facing in.
Lower to upper chest level and press back up.
Valid rep: full range of motion, no arching off the bench.
safety: Get the dumbbells into place by sitting with them on your thighs and kicking them up one at a time as you lie back.
To finish, bring the dumbbells to your chest and sit up, or lower them to the sides with control; do not drop them across your body.
Use a spotter for heavy attempts.
Stop at any shoulder or elbow pain.

form: Keep a slight fixed bend in the elbows throughout.
Lower until you feel a stretch in the chest, stopping before the shoulders roll forward.
Bring the dumbbells together in an arc over the upper chest.
Valid rep: same elbow angle throughout, controlled lowering.
safety: Avoid a true 1RM on flyes; the stretch puts the shoulders and pecs at risk. Prefer a 5-8 rep test or a heavy single.
Get the dumbbells into place by sitting with them on your thighs and kicking them up one at a time as you lie back.
Stop at any sharp pec or front shoulder pain.
Do not test with a recent pec or shoulder injury.

form: Lock the legs in the decline bench pads.
Keep a slight fixed bend in the elbows.
Lower in an arc to a comfortable stretch then bring the dumbbells together.
Valid rep: elbows do not straighten or bend more, controlled tempo.
safety: Avoid a true 1RM on flyes; the stretch puts the shoulders and pecs at risk. Prefer a 5-8 rep test or a heavy single.
Get the dumbbells into place by lying back with them held at the chest; have a spotter hand them to you if possible.
Sit up slowly after the test to avoid dizziness.
Stop at any sharp pec or shoulder pain.

form: Center the bench between the low pulleys.
Keep a slight elbow bend and the shoulder blades retracted.
Lower to a chest stretch and bring the handles together over the chest.
Valid rep: elbows stay fixed, no jerking, controlled return.
safety: Avoid a true 1RM on flyes; the stretch puts the shoulders and pecs at risk. Prefer a 5-8 rep test or a heavy single.
Check the stack pins and cable clips, and return the handles slowly so the stacks do not slam.
Make sure the stacks are equal weight on both sides.
Stop at any pec or front shoulder pain.

form: Set the pulleys low and stand in a staggered stance.
Keep the elbows slightly bent and chest up.
Sweep the handles up and together in front of the upper chest.
Valid rep: no leaning back or using the legs, controlled return.
safety: Avoid a true 1RM on flyes; the stretch puts the shoulders and pecs at risk. Prefer a 5-8 rep test or a heavy single.
Check the stack pins and cable clips, and return the handles slowly so the stacks do not slam.
Stop at any pec or front shoulder pain.
Do not test with a recent shoulder injury.

form: Place an incline bench between the low pulleys.
Keep the shoulder blades back and a slight elbow bend.
Lower to a chest stretch and bring the handles together over the upper chest.
Valid rep: same elbow angle throughout, no jerking, controlled return.
safety: Avoid a true 1RM on flyes; the stretch puts the shoulders and pecs at risk. Prefer a 5-8 rep test or a heavy single.
Check the stack pins and cable clips, and return the handles slowly so the stacks do not slam.
Check the bench is centered and locked.
Stop at any shoulder or pec pain.

prep: Light single-arm crossovers x12 per side
form: Use a staggered stance and lean slightly forward with a braced core.
Keep the working elbow slightly bent and fixed.
Bring the hand to the midline of the body and hold briefly.
Valid rep: no twisting the torso, controlled return to shoulder level.
safety: Avoid a true 1RM on flyes; the stretch puts the shoulders and pecs at risk. Prefer a 5-8 rep test or a heavy single.
Check the stack pins and cable clips, and return the handles slowly so the stacks do not slam.
Test both arms with the same weight and standard.
Stop at any front shoulder or pec pain.

form: Hands wider than shoulder width, fingers pointing forward.
Body stays in a straight line from head to heels; no sagging hips or piking.
Lower until the chest is about a fist from the floor.
Valid rep: chest down to the bottom position and arms fully extended at the top.
safety: Count only strict reps and stop at technical failure, when the hips sag or range of motion shortens.
Lower under control; do not drop to the floor.
Wide hands stress the shoulders; stop at any front shoulder pain.
Do not test with a current wrist or shoulder injury.

prep: Wrist circles and wrist stretches 30 s
form: Pick one hand position (close or wide) and keep it the same every test.
Body stays in a straight line from head to heels; no sagging hips or piking.
Lower until the chest nearly touches the floor.
Valid rep: full depth and full arm lockout each time.
safety: Count only strict reps and stop at technical failure, when the hips sag or range of motion shortens.
Lower under control and do not bounce off the floor.
Stop at any wrist, elbow or shoulder pain.
Do not test with a recent upper body injury.

prep: Wrist circles and wrist stretches 30 s
form: Hands under the shoulders or slightly closer, elbows tucked along the ribs.
Body stays in a straight line from head to heels; no sagging hips or piking.
Lower until the chest is near the hands.
Valid rep: full depth and full lockout of the elbows.
safety: Count only strict reps and stop at technical failure, when the hips sag or range of motion shortens.
Close hands put more load on the wrists and elbows; stop at any pain there.
Lower under control; no bouncing.
Do not test with a current elbow or wrist injury.

form: Feet on a stable box or bench, hands slightly wider than shoulders.
Body stays in a straight line from head to heels; no sagging hips or piking.
Lower until the chest nearly touches the floor.
Valid rep: full depth and full lockout, same box height every test.
safety: Count only strict reps and stop at technical failure, when the hips sag or range of motion shortens.
Make sure the box or bench is stable and will not slide.
Stop at any shoulder or wrist pain.
Do not test with a recent shoulder injury.

form: Feet on a stable bench and hands under the shoulders or slightly wider.
Body stays in a straight line from head to heels; no sagging hips or piking.
Lower until the chest nearly touches the floor.
Valid rep: full depth and full lockout, same foot height every test.
safety: Count only strict reps and stop at technical failure, when the hips sag or range of motion shortens.
Use a bench that will not slide or tip.
Stop at any shoulder, elbow or wrist pain.
Do not test with a recent upper body injury.

form: Hands on the bench edge slightly wider than shoulder width.
Body stays in a straight line from head to heels; no sagging hips or piking.
Lower until the chest touches the edge of the bench.
Valid rep: chest touches and arms fully lock out.
safety: Count only strict reps and stop at technical failure, when the hips sag or range of motion shortens.
Use a sturdy bench, box or locked Smith bar that will not move, and keep the same height every test.
Stop at any wrist or shoulder pain.
Lower under control each rep.

form: Hands on the bar about shoulder width.
Body stays in a straight line from head to heels; no sagging hips or piking.
Lower until the chest touches the bar.
Valid rep: chest touches and arms fully lock out.
safety: Count only strict reps and stop at technical failure, when the hips sag or range of motion shortens.
Use a sturdy bench, box or locked Smith bar that will not move, and keep the same height every test.
Check the Smith bar is hooked and the safeties are set.
Stop at any wrist or shoulder pain.

form: Hands wider than shoulder width on the bar or bench.
Body stays in a straight line from head to heels; no sagging hips or piking.
Lower until the chest touches the bar or bench.
Valid rep: chest touches and arms fully lock out.
safety: Count only strict reps and stop at technical failure, when the hips sag or range of motion shortens.
Use a sturdy bench, box or locked Smith bar that will not move, and keep the same height every test.
Wide hands stress the shoulders; stop at any front shoulder pain.
Lower under control each rep.

form: Hands close together on the bar or bench, elbows tucked along the ribs.
Body stays in a straight line from head to heels; no sagging hips or piking.
Lower until the chest touches the hands.
Valid rep: chest touches and the elbows fully lock out.
safety: Count only strict reps and stop at technical failure, when the hips sag or range of motion shortens.
Use a sturdy bench, box or locked Smith bar that will not move, and keep the same height every test.
Stop at any elbow or wrist pain.
Lower under control each rep.

prep: Assisted ring dips with a band or feet x5
form: Start in a stable support with arms locked and rings turned slightly out.
Keep the rings close to the body and the elbows back.
Lower until the shoulders are just below the elbows.
Valid rep: control the depth, no kipping, full lockout at the top.
safety: Count only strict reps and stop at technical failure, when the rings shake badly or range of motion shortens.
Set the rings low enough to step down safely, and check straps and buckles before use.
Do not go deeper than your shoulders tolerate; stop at any front shoulder or chest pain.
Do not test with a recent shoulder or pec injury.

prep: Bench dips with bent knees x8
form: Hands on the bench edge, shoulder width, fingers forward.
Keep the back close to the bench and shoulders down.
Lower until the upper arms are about parallel to the floor.
Valid rep: same foot position every test, full lockout at the top.
safety: Count only strict reps and stop at technical failure.
Do not go deeper than parallel; deep bench dips stress the front of the shoulder.
Make sure the bench is stable and will not slide.
Stop at any front shoulder or wrist pain.

prep: 5 min easy cardio such as rowing
form: Place the V-bar securely over the pull-up bar with hands on each side of it.
Start from a dead hang with arms fully extended.
Pull until the chest nears the V-bar.
Valid rep: full extension at the bottom and chest to handle at the top, no kipping.
safety: Count only strict reps from a dead hang and stop at technical failure, when you start kipping or can't reach the top.
Check the V-bar is centered and will not slip off the bar.
Lower under control each rep; do not drop into the bottom.
Stop at any elbow or shoulder pain.

prep: 5 min easy cardio such as rowing
form: One palm faces you and one faces away, about shoulder width.
Start from a dead hang with arms straight.
Pull until the chin clears the bar.
Valid rep: chin over the bar and full extension at the bottom, no kipping.
safety: Count only strict reps from a dead hang and stop at technical failure, when you start kipping or can't reach the top.
Lower under control to protect the elbows and biceps.
Stop at any elbow, biceps or shoulder pain.
Do not test with a recent elbow injury.

form: Wide overhand grip and lean the head slightly forward.
Start from a dead hang with arms fully extended.
Pull until the bar is near the back of the neck.
Valid rep: full extension at the bottom and bar to neck level, no kipping.
safety: Behind-the-neck pull-ups stress the shoulders; only test if you have good shoulder mobility and no pain.
Count only strict reps from a dead hang and stop at technical failure, when you start kipping or can't reach the top.
Do not hit the neck on the bar; stop at any neck or shoulder pain.
Lower under control each rep.

prep: Band pull-aparts x15 and arm circles
Scapular pull-ups x8 from a dead hang
form: Wide overhand grip, chest up, slight lean back before each pull.
Pull toward one hand until the bar nearly reaches your upper chest, then lower fully and go to the other side.
Start each rep from a full hang with arms straight.
Count each side as one rep only if the chest reaches the bar without kicking.
No swinging or kipping; only the arms and back should move.
safety: Stop at technical failure: when you can no longer reach the bar on a side without kipping.
Lower under control to a full hang; never drop from the top.
Skip the test if you have shoulder, elbow or wrist pain or a recent upper-body injury.
Stop if you feel sharp pain in the shoulder or elbow, especially on the side you are leaning toward.
Check the bar is secure and use chalk if your grip is slipping.

prep: Thoracic extension over a foam roller, 1 min
Scapular pull-ups x8 and 2 easy sets of 3 chin-ups
form: Shoulder-width underhand grip, chest up and lean back from the start.
Keep the spine arched and head back as you pull.
A valid rep brings the lower chest or sternum to the bar, not just the chin over it.
Return to a full hang with straight arms each rep.
No kicking or swinging to get the chest up.
safety: Stop at technical failure: the first rep where your sternum cannot touch the bar cleanly.
Lower slowly; the arched, leaned-back position stresses the lower back and shoulders.
Skip the test with low-back, shoulder or elbow pain or a recent injury.
Stop if you feel a pinch in the front of the shoulder or sharp elbow pain.
Make sure the bar is secure and there is clear space behind you to step off.

prep: Band pull-aparts x15 and wrist circles
Dead hang on the bar 20 s, then towel hang 10-15 s
form: Drape two strong towels over the bar and grip each tightly at the same height.
Start from a full hang with arms straight and shoulders engaged.
Pull until your chin clears your hands or the bar.
Lower all the way to straight arms each rep.
No kipping or swinging; count only strict reps.
safety: Inspect towels for tears and make sure they cannot slide off the bar before you start.
Stop when your grip is about to fail; step down rather than dropping unexpectedly.
Have a box or step under you so you can get down safely when your grip goes.
Stop with sharp pain in the fingers, forearms or elbows (grip-heavy movement).
Skip the test if you have elbow tendon or finger injuries.

prep: 5 min easy rowing or jump rope
Band dislocates x10 and arm circles
Kip swings x10 and ring or bar dips x5
form: Use a controlled hollow-to-arch kip to generate swing, not a wild thrash.
Pull the bar or rings toward your hips and transition quickly over the top.
A valid rep finishes with arms locked out in support above the bar or rings.
Lower under control back to a hang before the next rep.
Keep a firm false or regular grip so you do not slip in the transition.
safety: Only test if you can already do several clean muscle-ups; this is not a skill to learn under fatigue.
Stop at technical failure: missed transitions or a chicken-wing (one arm over first) mean stop.
Skip the test with shoulder, elbow or wrist pain or a recent injury.
Stop if you feel pain in the front of the shoulder or chest in the deep dip position.
Use mats underneath and make sure there is clear space for the swing.

prep: Scapular retractions on the straps x10
1 easy set of 6-8 inverted rows at a higher angle
form: Set strap height and foot position before the test and keep them the same for future retests.
Body stays in a straight plank from heels to head; squeeze glutes and brace.
Pull until your chest reaches your hands, squeezing shoulder blades together.
Lower to fully straight arms every rep.
No hip sagging or hip-thrusting to finish a rep.
safety: Check anchor point, straps and buckles are secure and rated for your bodyweight before each set.
Stop at technical failure: when hips sag or the chest no longer reaches the hands.
Lower slowly; do not drop into the bottom position.
Stop with sharp shoulder, elbow or low-back pain.
Skip the test with a recent shoulder or back injury.

prep: Band push-downs x20 and arm circles
2-3 lighter sets of close-grip bench to groove the bar path
form: Shoulder-width or slightly narrower grip, feet planted, upper back tight on the bench.
Lower with elbows bending and drifting slightly forward, bar toward upper chest or chin.
Keep the wrists stacked over the elbows and the bar under control.
A valid rep has a controlled bottom and full lockout without bouncing.
Keep elbows tucked, not flared.
safety: Use a spotter or set safety pins/arms in a rack just above face level; this bar travels near your face and neck.
Do not use a thumbless grip.
Use collars on the bar.
Elbows take high stress: stop with any sharp elbow pain.
A true 1RM is not advisable for this hybrid lift; prefer a heavy single with perfect form, or a 3-5 rep test.
Stop at the first form breakdown such as bouncing or elbows flaring.

prep: Band pull-aparts x15 and push-ups x10
Build up in 3-4 warm-up sets on the Smith machine
form: Position the bench so the bar touches your lower chest at the bottom.
Grip about shoulder width; too narrow strains the wrists.
Keep elbows tucked close to the body as you lower.
Touch the chest lightly and press to full lockout; no bouncing.
Keep shoulder blades pinned and feet planted.
safety: Set the machine's safety stops just below chest height so you can rest the bar if you fail.
Practice rotating the bar to re-hook it before you test.
Check the bar glides smoothly and the hooks engage.
Stop with wrist, elbow or shoulder pain.
Skip the test with a recent shoulder or elbow injury.
A spotter is still recommended for a true max.

prep: Band push-downs x20 and arm circles
2-3 lighter sets building toward working weight
form: Grip the inner angled handles of the EZ bar; lie with feet planted and upper back tight.
Lower the bar under control to the lower chest with elbows tucked.
Press back to full lockout over the chest.
Touch lightly, no bouncing off the chest.
Keep wrists straight, stacked over the elbows.
safety: Use a spotter or safety arms set just below chest level.
Never use a thumbless grip.
Use collars; an EZ bar can tip if loaded unevenly.
Stop with sharp elbow, wrist or shoulder pain.
Skip the test with a recent pec, shoulder or elbow injury.

prep: Overhead triceps stretch 2 x 20 s per arm
form: Close grip, lie on a flat bench, start with arms angled slightly back over the head.
Keep upper arms fixed and elbows in; only the forearms move.
Lower the bar behind the head in an arc to a full stretch, then extend.
A valid rep is a full lockout without moving the upper arms or bridging.
safety: A true 1RM is not advisable for this isolation lift; prefer a heavy single with perfect form, or a 3-5 rep test.
Have a spotter hand off and take the bar; it travels over your face and head.
Use collars on the bar.
Elbows are most at risk: stop with any sharp pain at the elbow.
Stop at the first form breakdown (swinging, shortened range, elbows drifting) and log the last clean rep.
Skip the test with elbow tendon pain or a recent injury.

form: Grip the inner handles of the EZ bar and lie on a flat bench.
Start with arms vertical over the chest.
Lower in an arc, upper arms still and elbows in, until the bar lightly touches the chin.
Extend back to full lockout without bouncing off the chin.
safety: A true 1RM is not advisable for this isolation lift; prefer a heavy single with perfect form, or a 3-5 rep test.
Use a spotter to hand off and take the bar; it travels toward your face.
Use collars on the bar.
Stop with any sharp elbow pain.
Stop at the first form breakdown (swinging, shortened range, elbows drifting) and log the last clean rep.
Skip the test with a recent elbow or shoulder injury.

prep: Overhead triceps stretch 2 x 20 s per arm
2-3 light sets on the decline bench
form: Lock your legs securely under the decline bench pads.
Close grip, arms vertical, elbows in.
Lower slowly in an arc until the bar lightly touches the forehead.
Extend to full lockout keeping the upper arms still.
safety: A true 1RM is not advisable for this isolation lift; prefer a heavy single with perfect form, or a 3-5 rep test.
Have a spotter hand you the bar and take it back; do not swing it into position.
Use collars on the bar.
Bar travels to your forehead: never lower it fast or uncontrolled.
Stop with sharp elbow pain or any dizziness from the head-down position.
Stop at the first form breakdown (swinging, shortened range, elbows drifting) and log the last clean rep.

prep: Lat and overhead triceps stretch 2 x 20 s
form: Set the incline bench between 45 and 75 degrees and lie with back flat.
Grip slightly narrower than shoulders, arms extended in line with the torso.
Lower behind the head until forearms touch biceps, upper arms close to the head.
Extend to full lockout with upper arms still.
safety: A true 1RM is not advisable for this isolation lift; prefer a heavy single with perfect form, or a 3-5 rep test.
Have a spotter hand off and take the bar.
Use collars on the bar.
Elbows and shoulders are most at risk in the deep stretch: stop with sharp pain.
Stop at the first form breakdown (swinging, shortened range, elbows drifting) and log the last clean rep.
Skip the test with a recent elbow or shoulder injury.

prep: Band dislocates x10 and band push-downs x20
Overhead triceps stretch 2 x 20 s per arm
form: Stand tall with glutes and abs braced; ribs down, no low-back arch.
Narrow overhand grip, arms locked overhead.
Lower behind the head with upper arms still and close to the head.
A valid rep returns to full lockout overhead without leaning back.
safety: A true 1RM is not advisable for this isolation lift; prefer a heavy single with perfect form, or a 3-5 rep test.
Clean or press the bar overhead with a light-to-moderate load only; getting a heavy bar overhead is itself risky.
Use collars on the bar.
Stop with sharp elbow or shoulder pain, or if your lower back starts arching.
Stop at the first form breakdown (swinging, shortened range, elbows drifting) and log the last clean rep.
If you fail, lower the bar to the front, not behind your head.

form: Weight is logged per dumbbell.
Lie on a flat bench with dumbbells over the shoulders, palms facing in.
Lower toward the sides of the head keeping upper arms still.
Extend to full lockout without letting the elbows flare.
safety: A true 1RM is not advisable for this isolation lift; prefer a heavy single with perfect form, or a 3-5 rep test.
Bring dumbbells up by sitting with them on your thighs and rolling back; lower them the same way.
Do not drop dumbbells beside your head; lower them to your chest before setting them down.
Stop with sharp elbow pain.
Stop at the first form breakdown (swinging, shortened range, elbows drifting) and log the last clean rep.

prep: Overhead triceps stretch 2 x 20 s per arm
2-3 light sets on the decline bench
form: Weight is logged per dumbbell.
Secure your legs under the decline pads before taking the dumbbells.
Lower toward the sides of the head with upper arms still and elbows in.
Extend fully to lockout over the shoulders.
safety: A true 1RM is not advisable for this isolation lift; prefer a heavy single with perfect form, or a 3-5 rep test.
Have a spotter hand you the dumbbells on the decline bench.
When done, bring the dumbbells to the chest and hand them off or lower them carefully; never drop overhead.
Stop with sharp elbow pain or dizziness from the head-down position.
Stop at the first form breakdown (swinging, shortened range, elbows drifting) and log the last clean rep.

prep: Overhead triceps stretch 2 x 20 s per arm
form: Sit upright on a bench with back support, feet planted.
Hold one dumbbell with both hands cupping the top plate.
Lower behind the head until forearms touch biceps, elbows pointing up.
Extend to lockout without arching the lower back.
safety: A true 1RM is not advisable for this isolation lift; prefer a heavy single with perfect form, or a 3-5 rep test.
Check the dumbbell head is tight before use; it is held above your head.
Have a spotter hand the dumbbell to you overhead when it is heavy.
When done, lower it to the front and onto your thighs, never behind you.
Stop with sharp elbow or shoulder pain.
Stop at the first form breakdown (swinging, shortened range, elbows drifting) and log the last clean rep.

prep: Overhead triceps stretch 2 x 20 s per arm
form: Stand hip-width, hold the kettlebell by the horns.
Brace abs, ribs down, upper arms vertical and close to the head.
Lower behind the head as far as shoulder mobility allows.
Extend to lockout without arching the lower back.
safety: A true 1RM is not advisable for this isolation lift; prefer a heavy single with perfect form, or a 3-5 rep test.
Press the kettlebell overhead with a load you can safely control.
Grip the horns firmly; a slipping bell behind the head is dangerous.
Stop with sharp elbow or shoulder pain or if the lower back arches.
Stop at the first form breakdown (swinging, shortened range, elbows drifting) and log the last clean rep.
When finished, lower the bell to the front before setting it down.

prep: Overhead triceps stretch 2 x 20 s per arm
form: Sit on a back-supported bench or stand tall with abs braced.
Upper arm vertical and next to the head; support it with the other hand if needed.
Lower behind the head to a full stretch, then extend to lockout.
Upper arm stays still; no leaning to the side.
safety: A true 1RM is not advisable for this isolation lift; prefer a heavy single with perfect form, or a 3-5 rep test.
Clean the dumbbell to shoulder height before extending overhead; avoid heavy loads you cannot control.
Lower the dumbbell to the front and onto your thigh when done.
Stop with sharp elbow or shoulder pain.
Stop at the first form breakdown (swinging, shortened range, elbows drifting) and log the last clean rep.

prep: Overhead triceps stretch 2 x 20 s per arm
form: Stand tall, feet hip-width, abs and glutes braced.
Upper arm vertical next to the head.
Lower behind the head to a full stretch with upper arm still.
Extend to lockout without leaning or arching the lower back.
safety: A true 1RM is not advisable for this isolation lift; prefer a heavy single with perfect form, or a 3-5 rep test.
Lift the dumbbell overhead with a load you can safely control.
Lower it to the front and down when done; never drop it behind you.
Stop with sharp elbow, shoulder or low-back pain.
Stop at the first form breakdown (swinging, shortened range, elbows drifting) and log the last clean rep.

form: Face away from the stack in a staggered stance, slight forward lean.
Elbows pointing forward/up, close to the head.
Extend fully to lockout, then return slowly to a full stretch.
Upper arms stay still; do not turn it into a press.
safety: A true 1RM is not advisable for this isolation lift; prefer a heavy single with perfect form, or a 3-5 rep test.
Check the rope and clip are secure and the pin is fully inserted in the stack.
Use a stable staggered stance so the cable does not pull you backward.
At failure, step forward to unload the stack under control.
Stop with sharp elbow or shoulder pain.
Stop at the first form breakdown (swinging, shortened range, elbows drifting) and log the last clean rep.

prep: 2 light sets on the low pulley
form: Rope on a low pulley; face away with hands behind the head and elbows up.
Stagger your stance and lean slightly away for stability.
Extend fully overhead keeping upper arms still.
Return slowly to the stretch; no jerking.
safety: A true 1RM is not advisable for this isolation lift; prefer a heavy single with perfect form, or a 3-5 rep test.
Check the rope, clip and stack pin are secure.
Set yourself before lifting the stack so the cable does not yank your arms back.
Stop with sharp elbow or shoulder pain.
Stop at the first form breakdown (swinging, shortened range, elbows drifting) and log the last clean rep.

prep: Wrist circles and light band push-downs x20
form: Underhand grip on a straight or EZ bar attachment, elbows pinned to the sides.
Stand tall with a slight forward lean; no shoulder movement.
Push down to full lockout and squeeze.
Return slowly until forearms are just above parallel.
safety: A true 1RM is not advisable for this isolation lift; prefer a heavy single with perfect form, or a 3-5 rep test.
Check the attachment clip and stack pin are secure.
The underhand grip stresses the wrists: stop with wrist or elbow pain.
Do not lean over the bar to push it down with bodyweight.
Stop at the first form breakdown (swinging, shortened range, elbows drifting) and log the last clean rep.

prep: Wrist circles and forearm stretches 20 s each
2 light sets on the preacher bench
form: Weight is logged per dumbbell.
Armpits snug against the top of the pad, upper arms flat on it.
Curl both dumbbells together; lower slowly to nearly straight arms.
No lifting the elbows off the pad or rocking the torso.
safety: A true 1RM is not advisable for this isolation lift; prefer a heavy single with perfect form, or a 3-5 rep test.
Have a partner hand you the dumbbells on the pad, or pick them up from the floor beside the bench carefully.
Never let the weight drop into full lockout at the bottom; this overloads the biceps tendon.
Stop with sharp pain at the front of the elbow, a classic biceps tendon warning sign.
Stop at the first form breakdown (swinging, shortened range, elbows drifting) and log the last clean rep.

prep: Wrist circles and forearm stretches 20 s each
form: Weight is logged per dumbbell.
Armpit snug on the pad, upper arm flat on it.
Curl up fully, then lower slowly to nearly straight.
Keep the shoulder down; no leaning back.
safety: A true 1RM is not advisable for this isolation lift; prefer a heavy single with perfect form, or a 3-5 rep test.
Use your free hand to steady the dumbbell when getting into and out of position.
Never drop into a hard lockout at the bottom; it strains the biceps tendon.
Stop with sharp pain at the front of the elbow.
Stop at the first form breakdown (swinging, shortened range, elbows drifting) and log the last clean rep.

prep: Wrist circles and forearm stretches 20 s each
form: Chest against the vertical side of the preacher bench, upper arms hanging straight down.
Shoulder-width underhand grip.
Curl to full contraction and lower to straight arms under control.
No swinging or using the legs.
safety: A true 1RM is not advisable for this isolation lift; prefer a heavy single with perfect form, or a 3-5 rep test.
Balance the bar securely on the seat before getting into position, and use collars.
Lower the bar back to the seat or floor under control when done.
Stop with sharp elbow or forearm pain.
Stop at the first form breakdown (swinging, shortened range, elbows drifting) and log the last clean rep.

prep: Wrist circles and forearm stretches 20 s each
form: Set the seat so armpits rest at the top of the pad and elbows line up with the machine's pivot.
Curl to full contraction, then lower under control to nearly straight.
Elbows stay on the pad; no rising off the seat.
safety: A true 1RM is not advisable for this isolation lift; prefer a heavy single with perfect form, or a 3-5 rep test.
Set the seat height and check the weight pin is fully inserted before testing.
Do not let the stack slam or yank your arms straight at the bottom.
Stop with sharp pain at the front of the elbow.
Stop at the first form breakdown (swinging, shortened range, elbows drifting) and log the last clean rep.

prep: Wrist circles and forearm stretches 20 s each
form: Place the preacher bench in front of a low pulley and set up with armpits on the pad.
Curl to full contraction, lower slowly to nearly straight.
Elbows stay on the pad; no rocking back.
safety: A true 1RM is not advisable for this isolation lift; prefer a heavy single with perfect form, or a 3-5 rep test.
Check the bar attachment clip and stack pin are secure.
Control the bottom; do not let the cable pull your elbows into hyperextension.
Stop with sharp pain at the front of the elbow.
Stop at the first form breakdown (swinging, shortened range, elbows drifting) and log the last clean rep.

prep: Wrist circles and forearm stretches 20 s each
form: Stand tall facing the low pulley, elbow pinned at your side.
Curl to full contraction, lower to a full stretch under control.
No leaning back or shoulder swing.
safety: A true 1RM is not advisable for this isolation lift; prefer a heavy single with perfect form, or a 3-5 rep test.
Check the handle clip and stack pin are secure.
Brace with your free hand on a stable support if needed.
Stop with sharp elbow or shoulder pain.
Stop at the first form breakdown (swinging, shortened range, elbows drifting) and log the last clean rep.

prep: Wrist circles and forearm stretches 20 s each
form: Rope on a low pulley, neutral grip, elbows pinned at the sides.
Curl to full contraction, lower to full extension under control.
Stand tall; no leaning back or hip drive.
safety: A true 1RM is not advisable for this isolation lift; prefer a heavy single with perfect form, or a 3-5 rep test.
Check the rope, clip and stack pin are secure.
Stand close enough that the stack does not pull you forward.
Stop with sharp elbow or forearm pain.
Stop at the first form breakdown (swinging, shortened range, elbows drifting) and log the last clean rep.

prep: Wrist circles and forearm stretches 20 s each
form: Grip the inner angled handles, stand tall with abs and glutes braced.
Elbows stay at your sides; curl to full contraction.
Start each rep from straight arms.
No leaning back or swinging with the hips.
safety: A true 1RM is not advisable for this isolation lift; prefer a heavy single with perfect form, or a 3-5 rep test.
Use collars on the bar.
Stop if you start leaning back to finish reps; this loads the lower back.
Stop with sharp pain at the front of the elbow or wrist.
Stop at the first form breakdown (swinging, shortened range, elbows drifting) and log the last clean rep.

prep: Wrist circles and forearm stretches 20 s each
form: Grip narrower than shoulder width, palms up, stand tall and braced.
Elbows stay at your sides; curl to full contraction.
Start each rep from straight arms.
No body swing or hip drive.
safety: A true 1RM is not advisable for this isolation lift; prefer a heavy single with perfect form, or a 3-5 rep test.
Use collars on the bar.
The narrow straight-bar grip can strain wrists: stop with wrist pain.
Stop if you have to lean back to complete a rep; protect the lower back.
Stop at the first form breakdown (swinging, shortened range, elbows drifting) and log the last clean rep.

prep: Wrist circles and forearm stretches 20 s each
form: Grip wider than shoulder width, palms up, stand tall and braced.
Elbows stay close to the sides; curl to full contraction.
Start each rep from straight arms.
No swinging or leaning back.
safety: A true 1RM is not advisable for this isolation lift; prefer a heavy single with perfect form, or a 3-5 rep test.
Use collars on the bar.
Stop with pain at the front of the elbow or shoulder.
Stop if you start leaning back to finish reps.
Stop at the first form breakdown (swinging, shortened range, elbows drifting) and log the last clean rep.

prep: Wrist circles and forearm stretches 20 s each
form: Shoulder-width underhand grip, stand tall.
Drag the bar up the front of the torso while the elbows travel back.
Curl to full contraction and lower along the same path.
No swinging or leaning back.
safety: A true 1RM is not advisable for this isolation lift; prefer a heavy single with perfect form, or a 3-5 rep test.
Use collars on the bar.
Stop with pain in the front of the shoulder from the elbows-back position.
Stop with sharp elbow pain.
Stop at the first form breakdown (swinging, shortened range, elbows drifting) and log the last clean rep.

prep: Wrist circles and forearm stretches 20 s each
form: Lie face down on a high bench with upper chest at the edge, arms hanging straight down.
Keep upper arms vertical and still; only the forearms move.
Curl to full contraction and lower to straight arms.
safety: A true 1RM is not advisable for this isolation lift; prefer a heavy single with perfect form, or a 3-5 rep test.
Make sure the bench is high and stable enough that the bar clears the floor.
Have a partner hand you the bar, or pick it up carefully; use collars.
When done, lower the bar to the floor under control before getting up.
Stop with sharp elbow pain.
Stop at the first form breakdown (swinging, shortened range, elbows drifting) and log the last clean rep.

prep: Wrist circles and forearm stretches 20 s each
form: Keep your torso pressed against the incline bench throughout.
Upper arms stay still; only the forearms move.
Curl as high as possible, then lower all the way to straight arms.
safety: A true 1RM is not advisable for this isolation lift; prefer a heavy single with perfect form, or a 3-5 rep test.
Have a partner hand off the bar, or pick it up carefully; use collars.
Lower the bar under control to a safe position before getting off the bench.
Stop with sharp elbow or shoulder pain.
Stop at the first form breakdown (swinging, shortened range, elbows drifting) and log the last clean rep.

prep: Wrist circles and forearm stretches 20 s each
form: Weight is logged per dumbbell.
Sit upright on the end of a bench, back straight, feet planted.
Elbows stay at the sides; curl to full contraction.
Lower to fully straight arms each rep; no swinging.
safety: A true 1RM is not advisable for this isolation lift; prefer a heavy single with perfect form, or a 3-5 rep test.
Pick dumbbells up from the floor or rack before sitting, keeping your back straight.
Stop if you start rocking your torso to complete reps.
Stop with sharp pain at the front of the elbow.
Stop at the first form breakdown (swinging, shortened range, elbows drifting) and log the last clean rep.

prep: Wrist circles and forearm stretches 20 s each
form: Weight is logged per dumbbell.
Stand tall with neutral grip, elbows close to the torso.
Curl outward, turning palms up as the weights rise.
Lower and rotate back to neutral; no swinging.
safety: A true 1RM is not advisable for this isolation lift; prefer a heavy single with perfect form, or a 3-5 rep test.
Bring dumbbells up from the floor or rack with a neutral spine, and set them down the same way.
Stop with sharp pain at the elbow or front of the shoulder.
Stop if you need body English or leaning back to finish reps.
Stop at the first form breakdown (swinging, shortened range, elbows drifting) and log the last clean rep.

prep: Wrist circles and forearm stretches 20 s each
form: Weight is logged per dumbbell.
Sit upright on a bench, palms facing forward.
Curl the dumbbells up and slightly outward, keeping upper arms still.
Lower to fully straight arms each rep.
safety: A true 1RM is not advisable for this isolation lift; prefer a heavy single with perfect form, or a 3-5 rep test.
Bring dumbbells up from the floor or rack with a neutral spine, and set them down the same way.
Stop with sharp pain at the elbow or front of the shoulder.
Stop at the first form breakdown (swinging, shortened range, elbows drifting) and log the last clean rep.

prep: Wrist circles and forearm stretches 20 s each
Pec and front-shoulder doorway stretch 20 s
form: Weight is logged per dumbbell.
Lie back on the incline bench with arms hanging straight down.
Curl up and outward with palms up, upper arms still.
Lower to full extension each rep.
safety: A true 1RM is not advisable for this isolation lift; prefer a heavy single with perfect form, or a 3-5 rep test.
Sit down with dumbbells on your thighs before leaning back; sit up with them the same way.
The stretched position loads the front of the shoulder and biceps tendon: stop with sharp pain.
Do not let the weights drop into a jerk at the bottom.
Stop at the first form breakdown (swinging, shortened range, elbows drifting) and log the last clean rep.

prep: Wrist circles and forearm stretches 20 s each
form: Weight is logged per dumbbell.
Sit back on a 45-degree incline, arms hanging, palms forward.
Keep wrists bent back and hold the same hand position all the way up.
Curl both dumbbells together; lower slowly to full extension.
safety: A true 1RM is not advisable for this isolation lift; prefer a heavy single with perfect form, or a 3-5 rep test.
Sit down with the dumbbells on your thighs before leaning back; reverse to get out.
Stop with wrist pain from the bent-back wrist position.
Stop with sharp pain at the elbow or front of the shoulder.
Stop at the first form breakdown (swinging, shortened range, elbows drifting) and log the last clean rep.

prep: Wrist circles and forearm stretches 20 s each
form: Weight is logged per dumbbell.
Lie chest-down on an incline bench, shoulders near the top, arms hanging straight.
Elbows stay in and still; curl to full contraction.
Lower to full extension each rep.
safety: A true 1RM is not advisable for this isolation lift; prefer a heavy single with perfect form, or a 3-5 rep test.
Pick up the dumbbells from the floor once you are in position, or have them handed to you.
Set them down on the floor under control before getting off the bench.
Stop with sharp elbow pain.
Stop at the first form breakdown (swinging, shortened range, elbows drifting) and log the last clean rep.

prep: Wrist circles and forearm stretches 20 s each
form: Weight is logged per dumbbell.
Bend at the hips with a flat back, free hand braced on a bench or thigh.
Working arm hangs straight down; curl toward the shoulder.
Upper arm stays still; lower to full extension.
safety: A true 1RM is not advisable for this isolation lift; prefer a heavy single with perfect form, or a 3-5 rep test.
Brace your free hand on something stable to protect the lower back.
Stop with low-back discomfort or sharp elbow pain.
Stop at the first form breakdown (swinging, shortened range, elbows drifting) and log the last clean rep.

prep: Wrist circles and forearm stretches 20 s each
form: Weight is logged per dumbbell.
Neutral grip, curl across the body toward the opposite shoulder.
Elbow stays close to the side; no shoulder swing.
Lower to fully straight arm each rep.
safety: A true 1RM is not advisable for this isolation lift; prefer a heavy single with perfect form, or a 3-5 rep test.
Bring dumbbells up from the floor or rack with a neutral spine, and set them down the same way.
Stop with sharp elbow or forearm pain.
Stop at the first form breakdown (swinging, shortened range, elbows drifting) and log the last clean rep.

prep: Wrist circles and forearm stretches 20 s each
form: Weight is logged per dumbbell.
Lie back on an incline bench, arms hanging, neutral grip.
Curl up keeping upper arms still.
Lower to full extension each rep.
safety: A true 1RM is not advisable for this isolation lift; prefer a heavy single with perfect form, or a 3-5 rep test.
Sit down with dumbbells on your thighs before leaning back; reverse to get out.
Stop with sharp elbow or front-shoulder pain.
Stop at the first form breakdown (swinging, shortened range, elbows drifting) and log the last clean rep.

prep: Wrist circles and forearm stretches 20 s each
2 light sets on the preacher bench
form: Weight is logged per dumbbell.
Armpits snug on the pad, upper arms flat, neutral grip.
Curl to full contraction; lower slowly to nearly straight.
Elbows stay on the pad.
safety: A true 1RM is not advisable for this isolation lift; prefer a heavy single with perfect form, or a 3-5 rep test.
Have the dumbbells handed to you or pick them up carefully beside the bench.
Never drop into a hard lockout at the bottom.
Stop with sharp elbow pain.
Stop at the first form breakdown (swinging, shortened range, elbows drifting) and log the last clean rep.

prep: Wrist circles and forearm stretches 20 s each
form: Weight is logged per dumbbell.
Curl up with palms up, rotate to palms down at the top.
Lower slowly with palms down, rotate back at the bottom.
Elbows stay at the sides; no swinging.
safety: A true 1RM is not advisable for this isolation lift; prefer a heavy single with perfect form, or a 3-5 rep test.
The weight you can lower palms-down is the limit: do not load beyond what you can control on the way down.
Bring dumbbells up from the floor or rack with a neutral spine, and set them down the same way.
Stop with sharp wrist, forearm or elbow pain.
Stop at the first form breakdown (swinging, shortened range, elbows drifting) and log the last clean rep.

prep: Wrist circles and forearm stretches 20 s each
form: Weight is logged per dumbbell.
Overhand (palms down) grip, stand tall, elbows at the sides.
Curl to full contraction; lower to straight arms.
Keep wrists straight; no swinging.
safety: A true 1RM is not advisable for this isolation lift; prefer a heavy single with perfect form, or a 3-5 rep test.
Bring dumbbells up from the floor or rack with a neutral spine, and set them down the same way.
Stop with wrist or outer-elbow pain.
Stop at the first form breakdown (swinging, shortened range, elbows drifting) and log the last clean rep.

prep: Wrist circles and forearm stretches 20 s each
2 light sets on the preacher bench
form: Overhand grip on the EZ bar, armpits on the pad.
Curl to full contraction; lower slowly to nearly straight.
Elbows stay on the pad; wrists straight.
safety: A true 1RM is not advisable for this isolation lift; prefer a heavy single with perfect form, or a 3-5 rep test.
Have the bar handed to you or rest it on the bench rack; use collars.
Never drop into a hard lockout at the bottom.
Stop with wrist or elbow pain.
Stop at the first form breakdown (swinging, shortened range, elbows drifting) and log the last clean rep.

prep: Wrist circles and forearm stretches 20 s each
form: Overhand grip on a bar attachment at the low pulley, elbows at the sides.
Curl to full contraction; lower to full extension under control.
Stand tall; no leaning back.
safety: A true 1RM is not advisable for this isolation lift; prefer a heavy single with perfect form, or a 3-5 rep test.
Check the attachment clip and stack pin are secure.
Stop with wrist or outer-elbow pain.
Stop at the first form breakdown (swinging, shortened range, elbows drifting) and log the last clean rep.

prep: Band pull-aparts x15 and arm circles
Lat stretch 2 x 20 s per side
2-3 lighter sets building to the test weight
form: Grab the opposite high-pulley handles so arms are crossed overhead, palms forward.
Chest up, slight arch, pull down in an arc.
Rotate palms to face each other at the bottom.
Return slowly to a full stretch each rep.
safety: A true 1RM is not advisable for this awkward cable movement; prefer a heavy single with perfect form, or a 3-5 rep test.
Check both handle clips and stack pins are secure.
Use a stable seat or stance so you are not lifted off it at heavy loads.
Stop with sharp shoulder pain, especially at the top stretch.
Stop at the first form breakdown (swinging, shortened range, elbows drifting) and log the last clean rep.

prep: Lat stretch 2 x 20 s per side
2-3 lighter sets building to the test weight
form: Set the thigh pad so your legs are locked in snugly.
Start from a full stretch with arms straight.
Lean back slightly, chest up, pull the V-bar to the upper chest.
Return to full extension under control; no jerking.
safety: Set the thigh pad snug before the test; it keeps you from being lifted off the seat.
Check the V-bar clip and stack pin are secure.
Count only reps with no excessive lean-back or momentum.
Stop with sharp shoulder or elbow pain.
At failure, let the bar rise slowly to the top; do not let go.

prep: Lat stretch 2 x 20 s per side
2-3 lighter sets building to the test weight
form: Set the thigh pad snug; grip the bar shoulder-width with palms facing you.
Start from straight arms, chest up, slight lean back.
Pull the bar to the upper chest, driving elbows down.
Return to full extension under control.
safety: Set the thigh pad so you are not lifted off the seat at heavy loads.
Check the bar clip and stack pin are secure.
The underhand grip loads the biceps tendon: stop with sharp pain at the front of the elbow.
Count only reps with no jerking or excessive lean-back.
At failure, return the bar overhead slowly; never let it fly up.

prep: 5 min easy rowing or arm bike
Band pull-aparts and band dislocates x15
Wall slides x10 to check overhead shoulder mobility
form: Lock thighs firmly under the knee pad before the pull.
Use a grip only moderately wider than shoulders; very wide grips stress the shoulder more.
Lean the head slightly forward and pull only to the top of the neck, never forcefully lower.
Drive elbows down and in; keep the torso upright without swinging.
A valid rep starts from straight arms and reaches the base of the neck without jerking.
safety: Behind-the-neck pulling stresses the shoulder joint; prefer a 3-5 rep test or test the front pulldown instead.
Skip this test if you lack pain-free overhead and external-rotation mobility or have shoulder or neck issues.
Stop immediately at any pinching in the front of the shoulder or neck pain.
Never let the bar drop onto the back of your neck; control the return to the top.
Check that the cable, clip and bar attachment are secure before heavy sets.

prep: 5 min easy rowing or arm bike
Single-arm band pulldowns x15 each side
form: Set the knee pad so your thighs are pinned and you cannot lift off the seat.
Start with the arm fully extended and the shoulder reaching up.
Pull the elbow down to your side; avoid twisting or leaning the torso to finish.
Keep the shoulder down and back rather than shrugging at the bottom.
A valid rep reaches the elbow to the ribs with a controlled return.
safety: Unilateral isolation-style lift; prefer a heavy 3-5 rep test and stop at the first form breakdown.
Let the weight return under control; do not let the stack yank the arm overhead.
Stop if you feel sharp shoulder, elbow or biceps tendon pain.
Check the handle clip and cable are secure; test both sides for balance.

form: Brace the trunk and keep a neutral spine; do not round forward to grab the handle.
Row the elbow back close to the body while keeping shoulders square.
Limit torso rotation and rocking; the back stays roughly upright.
A valid rep goes from a straight arm to the handle at the side of the torso.
safety: One-arm isolation-style lift; prefer a 3-5 rep test over a true single and stop at form breakdown.
Lower the weight under control; never let the stack pull you forward into spinal flexion.
Stop at any lower-back pain or sharp shoulder pain.
Set feet firmly on the platform and check the cable clip before heavy sets.

prep: Thoracic extensions over a foam roller
form: Make sure the platform is stable and does not slide on the seat.
Start with a long stretch but keep the lower back neutral, not rounded.
Pull the handle to the lower ribs, squeezing shoulder blades together.
Keep the torso near upright; minimal rocking counts as cheating.
A valid rep reaches the handle to the torso with a controlled return.
safety: The extra stretch loads the lower back; do not round to reach, and stop at the first form breakdown.
Prefer a heavy 3-5 rep test rather than a true single on this variation.
Use a non-slip platform secured on the seat; skip the test if it wobbles.
Stop at any lower-back pain or sharp shoulder pain.

prep: Hip hinges with a dowel x10
Light biceps curls x12 to warm the elbows
form: Hinge to a fixed torso angle with a neutral, braced spine.
Use a shoulder-width underhand grip; keep wrists straight.
Pull the bar to the lower abdomen with elbows close to the body.
The torso angle must stay the same; heaving up with the hips is not a valid rep.
Lower to full arm extension each rep.
safety: Underhand rowing stresses the biceps tendon; stop at any sharp pain in the elbow crease or upper arm.
Stop if the lower back rounds or you feel back pain; set the bar down rather than fight it.
Use collars and bumper plates; to bail, lower the bar to the floor under control.
Do not test with a recent back, biceps or elbow injury.

prep: Hip hinges with a dowel x10
form: Set the safety stops just below your lowest reach so the bar cannot fall to the floor.
Hinge to a fixed torso angle with a braced, neutral spine.
Pull the bar to the lower ribs or upper abdomen, elbows driving back.
Stand so the fixed bar path lines up with your pull; do not reach forward.
Keep the torso angle constant; heaving with the hips is not a valid rep.
safety: Set the safety stops before loading so a failed rep lands on them.
Know how to rotate the bar to hook it; practise re-racking with light weight.
Stop if your lower back rounds or you feel back pain.
Check the bar slides smoothly and the hooks engage before heavy sets.

prep: Hip hinges with a dowel x10
Light rows with the empty bar x10
form: Anchor the bar end in a corner or landmine so it cannot slide.
Hinge to a fixed torso angle with a braced, neutral spine.
Grip just behind the plates and pull the bar toward the chest.
Keep the torso angle constant; standing up to finish the rep does not count.
safety: Make sure the bar end is fully secured; a sliding bar can injure you or others.
Use collars on the loaded end so plates cannot slide off.
Stop if your lower back rounds or you feel back pain; set the bar down under control.
Do not test with a recent lower-back injury.

prep: Light set on the machine x12
form: Set the step or leg height so the top of the pad is at your upper chest.
Keep the chest on the pad throughout; do not lift off to heave.
Pull handles until elbows pass the torso, squeezing shoulder blades.
A valid rep goes from straight arms to full retraction with chest still on the pad.
safety: Check the load is evenly distributed and the plate horns have collars if available.
Know how to re-engage the support lever before you start; lower fully before releasing.
Stop at sharp shoulder pain or chest discomfort against the pad.
Lower the weight under control; do not drop the lever arm.

prep: Hip hinges with a dowel x10
form: Anchor the bar in a landmine or corner so it cannot slide.
Take a staggered, bent-knee stance with hips back and a braced, neutral spine.
Grip close to the collar and row the elbow back toward the hip.
Limit torso rotation; twisting to lift the weight is not a valid rep.
safety: Unilateral rows are a poor fit for true maxes; prefer a heavy 3-5 rep test and stop at form breakdown.
Use the legs to pick up and set down the bar; never round the back to grab it.
Stop at any lower-back or sharp shoulder pain.
Secure the bar end and use collars on the loaded end.

prep: Hip hinges with a dowel x10
Open-book thoracic rotations x8 each side
form: Anchor the bar end in a corner or landmine so it cannot slide.
Hinge with a braced, neutral spine; the free hand can brace on the knee.
Row the bar toward the lower ribs with the elbow close to the body.
Keep shoulders square; rotating the torso to finish is not a valid rep.
safety: Prefer a heavy 3-5 rep test over a true single for this unilateral row; stop at the first form breakdown.
Secure the bar end and collar the plates before lifting.
Stop at any lower-back pain or if the spine starts to round.
Set the bar down under control between sides; do not drop it.

form: Hinge with hips back and a flat, braced back; brace the free hand on a knee or bench if allowed.
Row the bell to the hip, retracting the shoulder blade.
Keep the hips and shoulders square; do not twist to lift.
A valid rep starts from a full hang and finishes with the bell at the torso.
safety: Kettlebells come in big jumps; prefer a heavy 3-5 rep test and stop at the first form breakdown.
Pick up and set down the bell with a hip hinge, never a rounded back.
Check the handle is dry and smooth; use chalk if grip slips.
Stop at any lower-back pain or sharp shoulder pain.

form: Set feet between the bells, hinge with hips back and a flat, braced back.
Row both bells to the stomach, retracting both shoulder blades.
Keep the torso angle fixed; standing up to row is not a valid rep.
Lower to a full hang each rep.
safety: The lower back works hard to hold the hinge; stop the moment it rounds.
Pick up and set down the bells with a hip hinge and good posture.
Prefer a heavy 3-5 rep test since kettlebell weight jumps are large.
Stop at any lower-back pain; do not test with a recent back injury.

form: Hinge with hips back and a flat, braced back, holding both bells.
Row one bell while the other stays in a full hang.
Resist torso twisting as the load shifts side to side.
A valid rep is one full row on each side with the torso angle unchanged.
safety: Not suited to a true max; use a heavy 3-5 rep test and stop at the first form breakdown.
Pick up and set down the bells with a hip hinge; never round to grab them.
Stop at any lower-back pain or if your back starts to round.
Use chalk and check handles if grip is slipping.

prep: Prone Y-T raises on the bench x8
form: Set the bench at about 30-45 degrees and keep the chest on the pad.
Row the dumbbells to your sides, squeezing the shoulder blades together.
Do not lift the chest off the pad to heave the weight.
A valid rep goes from straight arms to elbows past the torso.
safety: Weight is logged per dumbbell; pick dumbbells from the floor beside the bench before lying down.
Get set by sitting on the bench end, then lying forward with the dumbbells hanging.
To bail, lower the dumbbells to the floor beside you under control; do not drop them from height.
Prefer a 3-5 rep test over a true single and stop at the first form breakdown.
Check the bench is stable and locked at the chosen angle.

form: The thick axle does not rotate; set grip carefully, double overhand if able, or mixed grip.
Bar over mid-foot, take slack out, brace hard before the pull.
Keep the bar close and the back neutral from floor to lockout.
A valid rep finishes standing tall with hips and knees locked, no hitching.
safety: Use bumper plates and collars; if grip or form fails, lower the bar under control rather than drop it awkwardly.
Stop if your back rounds noticeably or you feel sharp back pain.
The axle is hard on the grip and biceps; avoid curling it with a mixed grip to protect the biceps tendon.
Do not test with a recent lower-back injury; check the axle sleeves and collars before lifting.

form: Set up in your clean start: shoulders over the bar, back fully extended, hips above knees.
Use a hook grip or double overhand; no mixed grip.
Push the floor away and keep the back angle constant until the bar passes the knees.
A valid rep is a smooth pull to full standing with the bar close and back neutral.
safety: Use bumper plates and collars on a platform.
Stop if the hips shoot up first or the back rounds; that is a failed rep.
Lower the bar under control; do not drop from the top unless on bumpers with clear space.
Do not test with lower-back pain or a recent hamstring strain.

form: Use a wide snatch grip with hook grip; straps are acceptable for heavy attempts.
Start with hips low, chest up and back fully extended.
Keep the bar close and the back angle constant past the knees.
A valid rep finishes standing tall with locked hips and knees.
safety: The wide grip makes the pull longer and harder on the back; stop at any rounding.
Use bumper plates and collars on a platform.
Stop at sharp back or hamstring pain; do not test with a recent back injury.
Lower the bar under control; keep the area clear.

prep: Hip hinges with a dowel x10
Light RDLs from the floor x8
form: Stand on a stable, non-slip platform no more than a few inches high.
Soft knees, push hips back, and keep the bar against the legs.
Lower only as far as you can keep a neutral back; that is your range.
A valid rep returns to full hip lockout without the back rounding.
safety: RDLs are rarely maxed; prefer a heavy 3-5 rep test and stop at the first form breakdown.
Stop at any rounding of the lower back or sharp hamstring pain.
Make sure the platform is stable and step off carefully between sets.
Do not test with a recent hamstring strain or lower-back injury; use collars.

form: Keep a slight, fixed knee bend; hinge at the hips.
Keep dumbbells close to the legs and the back neutral.
Lower only as far as hamstring flexibility allows without rounding.
A valid rep finishes standing tall with hips locked.
safety: Weight is logged per dumbbell; pick the dumbbells up from the floor or rack with a hinge and neutral back.
Prefer a heavy 3-5 rep test rather than a true single, stopping at the first form breakdown.
Stop if the lower back rounds or you feel hamstring pulling pain.
Set the dumbbells down under control; do not drop them near your feet.

prep: Hip hinges with a dowel x10
form: Start from the hooks at mid-thigh; unhook with a straight back.
Stand so the fixed bar path runs close to your thighs and shins.
Hinge with a slight knee bend, lowering only as far as you keep a neutral back.
A valid rep returns to full hip lockout.
safety: Set the safety stops just below your lowest point before loading.
Practise rotating the bar to re-hook it with light weight first.
Prefer a 3-5 rep test over a true single and stop at the first form breakdown.
Stop at lower-back rounding or sharp hamstring pain.

form: Take a wide stance with toes slightly out; knees track over toes.
Hips back, legs nearly straight, chest up and back flat.
Keep the bar close to the body throughout.
A valid rep finishes standing tall with hips locked.
safety: Stiff-legged pulls from the floor load the hamstrings and lower back; prefer a 3-5 rep test.
Stop at any back rounding, sharp hamstring or groin pain.
Use bumper plates and collars; lower the bar under control.
Do not test with a recent back, hamstring or adductor injury.

prep: Hip hinges with a dowel x10
form: Set up in a squat rack and place the bar low on the upper back, not on the neck.
Brace hard and keep the spine neutral as you hinge.
Push hips back with nearly straight legs; descend only to where the back stays flat.
A valid rep returns to full standing without the knees bending to cheat.
safety: Good mornings put high shear on the lower back; never test a true 1RM, use a 3-5 rep test with perfect form.
Set safety pins or straps at your lowest point so a failed rep can be dropped onto them.
Stop at any back rounding, back pain or hamstring pulling.
Use collars and do not test with a recent back injury.

prep: Hip hinges with a dowel x10
form: Set the pins so you start bent over near parallel with a neutral back.
Get under the bar with it low on the upper back, brace hard before driving up.
Drive hips forward to stand without rounding the back.
A valid rep starts dead from the pins and finishes fully upright.
safety: Prefer a 3-5 rep test over a true single; the lower back is at high risk.
If you cannot start the lift with a flat back, the weight is too heavy; abort.
Return the bar to the pins under control; use collars.
Stop at any lower-back pain and do not test with a recent back injury.

prep: Seated hip hinges with a dowel x10
form: Sit on a stable box inside a power rack with pins set as a safety.
Bar low on the upper back, shoulder blades squeezed, brace before bending.
Lean forward with a neutral spine only as far as you control.
A valid rep returns to fully upright without rounding.
safety: Never test a true 1RM; use a 3-5 rep test and stop at the first form breakdown.
Set rack pins so a failed rep can be lowered onto them.
Stop at any lower-back pain or rounding; skip testing with a recent back injury.
Check the box is stable and centred under you; use collars.

form: Use a stable block or plate under the balls of your feet.
Keep knees straight but not hyperextended; torso upright.
Lower to a full stretch and rise to full plantarflexion each rep.
A valid rep has a brief pause at the bottom with no bouncing.
safety: Calf raise maxes are low value; prefer a 3-5 rep test and stop at the first partial rep.
Check the block cannot slip, and know how to rotate the bar to re-rack.
Set the safety stops just below your shoulders' lowest position.
Stop at any Achilles or calf pain; do not test with Achilles tendon issues.

form: Unrack the bar from a squat rack with the bar on the upper back.
Stand tall with a braced trunk; keep knees straight.
Rise as high as possible on the toes and lower under control.
A valid rep reaches a full rise without bouncing or bending the knees.
safety: Balance is the limiting factor; prefer a 3-5 rep test over a true single and stop at the first form breakdown.
Work inside a squat rack with safety pins set just below the bar.
Stop at any Achilles or calf pain; avoid testing with Achilles tendon issues.
Use collars and re-rack the bar carefully after the set.

prep: Bodyweight calf raises and toe raises x15
form: Unrack the bar from a squat rack with it on the upper back.
Rock from heels (toes up) to full toe raise with control.
Keep the torso upright and knees straight; avoid using momentum.
A valid rep goes through the full rocking range under control.
safety: Not suited to maximal loads; prefer a 3-5 rep test and stop at the first loss of balance.
Work inside a squat rack with safety pins set just below the bar.
Stop at any Achilles, shin or calf pain.
Use collars and re-rack carefully.

form: Place only the balls of your feet on the bottom edge of the platform.
Keep knees straight but not locked hard; do not bend them to push.
Lower to a full stretch and press to full extension each rep.
A valid rep is full range with no bouncing.
safety: Never release the safety catches without a secure grip on the platform with your feet; keep them within reach.
If your feet slip, the sled can come down toward you; use the safeties and do not overload.
Prefer a 3-5 rep test over a true single; stop at the first partial rep.
Stop at any Achilles or calf pain; re-engage the safeties before getting out.

form: Adjust the seat so the knees are only slightly bent at the start.
Keep the balls of the feet firmly on the platform.
Press through the full range, lowering to a stretch each rep.
A valid rep is full range without bending the knees to help.
safety: Set the seat and check the weight pin is fully inserted before starting.
Prefer a 3-5 rep test over a true single and stop at the first partial rep.
Stop at any Achilles or calf pain; avoid testing with Achilles issues.
Lower the weight slowly; do not let the stack slam.

form: Position the pad on the lower back and hips, not the spine.
Brace the arms on the handles and keep the back flat.
Lower to a full stretch and rise to full toe extension.
A valid rep has no bouncing and the knees stay straight.
safety: Prefer a 3-5 rep test rather than a true single; stop at the first partial rep.
Make sure the machine is loaded evenly and the pad is set to your height.
Stop at any lower-back, Achilles or calf pain.
Step out carefully only after the lever is fully lowered.

form: Place a stable block about 12 inches in front of the bench and the balls of the feet on it.
Pad the bar so it sits comfortably above the knees, not on them.
Rise as high as possible and lower to a full stretch.
A valid rep is full range with no bouncing.
safety: Have a partner place and remove the bar, or use a seated calf machine instead.
Prefer a 3-5 rep test over a true single; stop at the first partial rep.
Check the block cannot slip; stop at any knee, Achilles or calf pain.
Use collars so plates cannot slide off the bar.

prep: Shoulder rolls and band pull-aparts x15
form: Pick the bar up from a rack at thigh height, not from the floor behind you.
Stand tall with arms straight and a pronated grip slightly wider than shoulders.
Shrug straight up toward the ears; do not roll the shoulders.
A valid rep has straight arms and a brief hold at the top.
safety: Prefer a 3-5 rep test over a true single and stop at the first form breakdown.
Use a rack set at thigh height to unrack and re-rack safely.
Straps are fine for grip, but stop at neck pain or tingling into the arms.
Use collars and do not test with neck or shoulder injuries.

prep: Shoulder rolls and band pull-aparts x15
Light shrugs on the Smith bar x12
form: Set the hooks at thigh height and stand with the bar behind you.
Unhook with arms straight and chest up.
Shrug straight up toward the ears, no arm bending or rolling.
A valid rep has a brief pause at the top and a controlled lowering.
safety: Set the safety stops just below the bar's lowest position.
Practise rotating the bar to re-hook it with light weight.
Prefer a 3-5 rep test over a true single; stop at the first form breakdown.
Stop at neck pain or tingling into the arms.

prep: Light set on the machine x12
form: Stand centred between the handles and brace before lifting.
Lift with the legs to stand upright before shrugging.
Shrug straight up with arms straight; avoid rolling.
A valid rep has a brief hold at the top.
safety: Prefer a 3-5 rep test over a true single; stop at the first form breakdown.
Lower the lever with your legs at the end, keeping the back neutral.
Check the plates are loaded evenly with collars if available.
Stop at neck pain or tingling into the arms.

prep: Light shrugs on the machine x12
form: Set the shoulder pads so you are standing straight with the pads resting on the shoulders.
Keep the torso upright and knees soft but not bending to help.
Shrug straight up toward the ears and lower under control.
A valid rep is full range with a pause at the top.
safety: Prefer a 3-5 rep test over a true single; stop at the first form breakdown.
Make sure the pads are padded and positioned on the shoulders, not the neck.
Stop at any neck pain, compression or tingling into the arms.
Check the weight pin is fully inserted before starting.

form: Stand close to the low pulley with a braced trunk.
Keep arms straight and shrug straight up toward the ears.
Avoid leaning back or using the legs.
A valid rep has a brief pause at the top and controlled lowering.
safety: Prefer a 3-5 rep test over a true single; stop at the first form breakdown.
Check the bar attachment and cable clip are secure.
Lower under control; do not let the stack yank your shoulders down.
Stop at neck pain or tingling into the arms.

form: Hold the bar behind you at arm's length with hands shoulder-width.
Let the bar roll toward the fingers, then curl the wrists up.
Keep arms straight; only the wrists should move.
A valid rep is full wrist range without elbow bending.
safety: Wrist curls are not suitable for a 1RM; use a 5-10 rep test and stop at the first form breakdown.
Use a rack to pick up the bar; avoid lifting it from the floor behind you.
Stop at any sharp wrist, elbow or finger pain.
Do not test with wrist or elbow tendon issues.

form: Rest forearms on the thighs or bench with wrists just past the edge.
Lower under control, then curl the wrists up fully.
Keep forearms in contact; do not lift the elbows to help.
A valid rep is full wrist range with controlled lowering.
safety: Wrist curls are not suited to a true 1RM; use a 5-10 rep test and stop at the first form breakdown.
Check the cable clip and bar attachment are secure.
Stop at any sharp wrist or elbow pain.
Return the bar to the floor under control at the end.

form: Rest forearms on the thighs with wrists just past the knees.
Lower the bar under control, then extend the wrists up.
Keep forearms in contact with the thighs.
A valid rep is full range without lifting the forearms.
safety: Wrist extensors are weak and injury-prone; use a 5-10 rep test, not a 1RM.
Stop at any sharp wrist or outer-elbow pain.
Do not test with tennis elbow or wrist injuries.
Use collars if using plates.

form: Kneel with forearms flat on the bench and wrists hanging over the edge.
Lower the bar under control, then extend the wrists up.
Keep forearms on the bench throughout.
A valid rep is full range with no forearm lift.
safety: Use a 5-10 rep test rather than a 1RM; wrist extensors are injury-prone.
Stop at any sharp wrist or outer-elbow pain.
Pad the knees and check the bench is stable.
Set the bar on the floor under control at the end.

form: Kneel with forearms flat on the bench and wrists just over the edge.
Let the dumbbells lower under control, then curl the wrists up.
Keep forearms on the bench; only the wrists move.
A valid rep is full range with controlled lowering.
safety: Weight is logged per dumbbell; use a 5-10 rep test rather than a 1RM.
Pick up the dumbbells one at a time before setting your forearms.
